La Liga stars Lamine Yamal and Vinicius Jr have publicly said they face racist abuse in Spain, which has faced FIFA punishment over the issue.
Weeks after FIFA punished Spain over Islamophobic chants by their supporters and their star Lamine Yamal admitted having repeatedly experienced racism in the country, the Spanish team’s head coach, Luis de la Fuente, has claimed the country does not have a racism problem.
De la Fuente appeared to quash any concerns about racism as he addressed the media on Saturday before his team’s UEFA Nations League match against England .
“In Spain, there is no racism,” the 65-year-old said in response to a question about his England counterpart Thomas Tuchel, who revealed he would speak to his players about the antiracism protocol in place before Sunday’s match in Madrid.
“You can tell this to Thomas. As clear as that. There is no racism. Exactly the same as in England, in Spain, there is no racism. We’re not racists, none of us.”
While a capacity crowd is expected for the top-of-the-table Group C clash at the Metropolitano Stadium, the world champions will have to play their next home friendly with a reduced capacity as a punishment for Spanish supporters singing an Islamophobic chant during a fixture against Egypt in March.
Several high-profile players have been targeted by racist abuse in recent years, including Yamal and Real Madrid’s Brazilian forward Vinicius Jr , who has been moved to tears in news conferences while talking about the issue.
England players faced racist abuse during a game in the Spanish capital in a 2004 friendly in which Black England players, including Ashley Cole and Shaun Wright-Phillips, were targeted.
Tuchel said he did not expect racist abuse on Sunday but his players ⁠⁠would be reminded of antiracism protocols.
“I think the referee and the officials know about that [racist chanting].”
He later clarified his comments as not being specifically about Spain and criticised reporters for creating “a lot of confusion for absolutely nothing”.
“I never talked about racism in Spain. I answered politely a question about what happens,” he said.
England midfielder Declan Rice said the squad knew exactly how to respond if racism occurred.
“In the past, I’ve experienced that in Montenegro, ‌‌Bulgaria, and there was a protocol in place we followed,” Rice told reporters. “We came off the pitch. We know exactly where we are as a group on that.
“I’m not expecting any of that. This is a beautiful city, great stadium. The players we’re playing against we have a lot of respect for. It’s set up to be a really good evening and hopefully not a negative one.”
In September, Barcelona and Spain star Yamal said he had experienced racism “a thousand ⁠⁠times” with ⁠⁠many people unaware that their comments or behaviour is racist.
Asked by former Argentina international Jorge Valdano in an interview with Spanish broadcaster Movistar whether he had directly experienced racism, Lamine said: “A thousand times.”
“People are indirectly ⁠⁠racist towards you but maybe don’t ⁠⁠realise it. There are a lot of comments or looks that are racist, and they don’t even notice.
“If someone calls me Black, it’s ⁠⁠not going to bother me at all. Ultimately I’m Black. I’m not any other ⁠⁠colour. Another thing is whether it’s ⁠⁠good or bad, whether they’re saying it to offend me.
“But if I’m playing a match. and they paid for a ticket to see ‌‌me, I’m not going to get angry just because they disrespected me.”
Yamal criticised the anti-Muslim chants by fans in what should have been a friendly match against Egypt.
A section of supporters had chanted: “Whoever doesn’t jump is Muslim.”
Egypt’s national anthem also received a barrage of whistles before the friendly.
Yamal, a Muslim whose father moved from Morocco to Spain, issued a damning statement on Instagram in the wake of the row.
“I am a Muslim. Yesterday at the stadium the chant ‘the one who doesn’t jump is the Muslim’ was heard,” he posted.
“I know I was playing for the rival team and it wasn’t something personal against me but as a Muslim person it doesn’t stop being disrespectful and something intolerable.”
Yamal added: “I understand not all fans are like this, but to those who sing these things, using a religion as a mockery on the field makes you ignorant and racist people.”
Real Madrid’s Vinicius has been the most notable target of racism and has openly addressed the issue, often in tearful news conferences.
On May 22, 2023, Vinicius said the Spanish league “now belongs to racists”, and two days later, Spanish police arrested four men suspected of hanging an effigy of him four months earlier from a bridge in Madrid in front of the club’s training centre in advance of a Madrid derby.
The arrests came amid an international outcry after racist abuse was hurled at Vinicius during another league match.
A year later, Vinicius broke down in tears and said he was struggling to stay motivated and enjoy playing football due to the recurring racist abuse he was subjected to in Spain.
During an emotional news conference before Brazil’s friendly against Spain, he expressed frustration that fans kept getting away with hurling racist abuse towards him.
This year, Vinicius praised Yamal for his public condemnation of Islamophobic chants, saying players need to stick together in the fight against discrimination.
“It’s important that Lamine speaks about it. It could help others. We are famous. We have money. We can balance these things better, but the poor people and the Black people who are everywhere, they surely struggle more than we do. So we have to stick together, those who have a stronger voice, the players.”
“I’m not saying that Spain or Germany or Portugal are racist countries, but there are racists in these countries and in Brazil and other countries as well,” Vinicius said. “But if we keep fighting together, I think future players and people in general won’t have to go through this again.”

Three men have been convicted of carrying out an attack on a church in the Karak governorate that killed nine people.
A Jordanian court has sentenced three men to death by hanging for carrying out last month’s deadly gun attack on a church in the kingdom’s south.
Gunmen killed nine people and wounded 25 others when they stormed a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Hammoud village, in Jordan’s Karak governorate on October 23.
Authorities said three men, two Jordanian brothers and their relative by marriage, had fled after the attack and were arrested three days later.
In a statement on Sunday, the Jordanian military said the “State Security Court issued its ruling sentencing to death the three criminals who carried out the terrorist attack” at the church.
The court found them guilty of “committing terrorist attacks” resulting in death, as well as weapons offences, “conspiracy to commit terrorist acts” and “promoting the ideas of a terrorist organisation”.
“One of the perpetrators of the terrorist operation was also convicted of providing funds with the intention of using them to finance the commission of terrorist acts,” it added.
In late October, Jordanian security forces arrested the three men suspected of the attack that targeted the St George’s Greek Orthodox church in Karak, after clashing with them.
The governorate is home to many members of Jordan’s Christian minority, which makes up about 300,000 of the country’s 11.5 million people.
King Abdullah II said those behind the attack would face the “harshest penalties” as he offered his condolences to the victims’ families. He has ordered a review of the country’s security procedures for responding to attacks after the incident.

Judge Noël Wise found buyers plausibly alleged the chipmakers conspired to cut conventional DRAM supply and shift capacity to HBM, distinguishing the Ninth Circuit's DRAM II.
A federal judge on Nov. 14 refused to dismiss a proposed class action accusing Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron of conspiring to restrict the supply of conventional dynamic random-access memory, or DRAM, the standardized memory chips used in computers, phones and servers.
U.S. District Judge Noël Wise of the Northern District of California denied the companies' joint motion to dismiss in full, finding the complaint plausibly alleged an agreement in violation of Section 1 of the Sherman Act. The allegations, accepted as true at this stage, have not been proven.
The companies argued the case was a rerun of DRAM II, in which the Ninth Circuit in 2022 affirmed dismissal of claims against the same three companies over a 2016–2018 supply restriction. "The Court finds that it is not," Judge Wise wrote.
The suit was filed June 25, 2026, by 17 consumers and small businesses from five states. It concerns conventional DRAM, which the complaint describes as "standardized memory built to industry specifications and sold for ordinary purposes," including DDR5 generation modules built for computers.
According to the complaint, the three companies controlled more than 91% of global DRAM revenue as of the third quarter of 2025. They allegedly cut production starting in late 2022 and, beginning in 2023, shifted capacity to high bandwidth memory, or HBM, a specialized DRAM product for artificial intelligence accelerators that "requires approximately three to four times the silicon wafer area per gigabyte compared to conventional DDR5 DRAM."
By the third quarter of 2025, conventional DRAM prices had risen 171.8% in one year, according to the complaint, which alleges a 697% increase over 18 months. Yet "not one of the three Defendants expanded or announced plans to meaningfully expand commodity DRAM production capacity," the complaint alleges.
Without direct evidence of an agreement, the plaintiffs needed plus factors, additional facts suggesting a preceding agreement rather than conscious parallelism, in which competitors independently make similar moves.
Judge Wise rejected the companies' argument that timing gaps undercut parallel action. SK Hynix and Micron announced cuts three weeks apart in late 2022, she noted, and Samsung's lag of about four and a half months, until April 7, 2023, was "not such an unreasonably long delay that it defeats an allegation of parallel conduct on a motion to dismiss."
She found the complaint plausibly alleged that the three companies acted in parallel when they cut supply, shifted production from conventional DRAM such as DDR5 to HBM, and wound down DDR4.
Under Ninth Circuit precedent, action against self-interest must be "so perilous in the absence of advance agreement that no reasonable firm would make the challenged move without such an agreement." Judge Wise wrote that a pivot to HBM by itself "might not be sufficient," but that "the related conduct tips this factor over the edge to weigh in Plaintiffs' favor."
According to the complaint, all three signed long-term contracts locking in HBM supply, Samsung and SK Hynix reportedly refused long-term agreements with major conventional DRAM customers, and Micron announced on Dec. 3, 2025, that it would close Crucial, its 30-year-old consumer brand. Those moves, which she called "difficult if not impossible to unwind," plus the failure to expand despite record prices, "are the sort that at the pleading stage, it appears no reasonable firm would make without a prior agreement," she wrote.
She applied similar reasoning to allegations that Samsung and Micron delayed or halted new DRAM plants, citing the Ninth Circuit's 1990 Petroleum Products decision that "Changes in refinery capacity are not readily reversible." "The Court views the commitment to build or not build manufacturing capacity as analogous," she wrote. She also counted the companies' alleged same-quarter 2025 decisions to wind down DDR4 as a plus factor, citing the complaint's allegation that "older, slower DDR4 came to cost more per gigabyte than newer, faster DDR5."
Judge Wise found that near-identical customer-vetting practices all three companies allegedly adopted in January 2026 "strongly support a plausible inference of conspiracy." She rejected the companies' "obvious and non-conspiratorial explanation" of booming AI demand, noting that the vetting began after the AI boom and the HBM pivot were underway.
The court gave no weight to three other arguments. Judge Wise held that investor statements, including Micron's 2022 reference to "supply discipline," did not distinguish the case from DRAM II. Though the conference-meeting allegations went beyond those in DRAM II, she wrote that DRAM II "seemingly all but forecloses a trial court from giving any weight to trade conference meetings" absent specifics, and she called the market's oligopolistic structure "neutral in the analysis."
According to the complaint, the companies and two other manufacturers formed a criminal cartel to fix DRAM prices from 1998 to 2002; Samsung paid a $300 million fine, Hynix paid $185 million, and Micron received immunity for cooperating as a whistleblower. Judge Wise, like the DRAM II court, rejected the argument that the now-20-year-old history should not count.
At the hearing, the companies quoted the late Judge Posner's line that competitors in concentrated markets "watch each other like hawks." Judge Wise wrote: "But Plaintiffs' allegations go beyond hawks watching each other; their contentions are more akin to hawks flying in formation – an activity that hawks ordinarily do not do."
The plaintiffs are represented by Bathaee Dunne LLP. Samsung is represented by O'Melveny & Myers LLP, SK Hynix by Cleary Gottlieb Steen & Hamilton LLP, and Micron by Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher LLP.
Judge Wise ordered the companies to answer by Dec. 7, 2026. Because the court had reset argument by about three weeks, she also granted the companies' unopposed administrative motion to continue early case deadlines and reset the initial case management conference for Jan. 12, 2027, at 9 a.m.

A senior Hamas figure who helped plan and oversee the 7 October 2023 attack on Israel has been killed in an Israeli airstrike, officials in Israel and Gaza have said.
Samir Abu Younis, the newly appointed commander of the Rafah Brigade, was killed on Saturday in Al-Mawasi in the southern Gaza Strip, according to Hamas's Al-Qassam Brigades military wing.
A local Hamas official confirmed Younis's death. The Israeli military said it had targeted him and that prior to the strike "steps were taken to mitigate harm to civilians".
Eyewitnesses in Gaza said four missiles struck a tent in the Al-Waha camp, which shelters hundreds of displaced people in Al-Mawasi, causing a fire to break out.
A medical source at Nasser Hospital in the southern city of Khan Younis said three injured people had arrived there, as well as a dead body.
The Israel Defence Forces (IDF) and Israel's security agency, the ISA, confirmed in a statement on Telegram that it had "eliminated" Younis.
Describing him as a "central figure among Hamas's senior figures", it said he had "acted with the aim of trying to restore the strength of the brigade and the Hamas terrorist organisation".
It added: "Younis directed the brigade's terrorists to advance and carry out terror attacks against Israeli civilians and IDF troops."
Al-Qassam Brigades wrote on Telegram that Younis had "participated in numerous high-profile operations and resisted enemy incursions", and was "one of the most important commanders involved in planning and overseeing the 7 October attack".
Younis, 53, had been in his position since 15 September, following the death of the brigade's previous commander, Nael Abu Obeid.
He joined Hamas' armed wing in 1991 and held several senior operational roles before becoming commander. His funeral will be held on Sunday afternoon in Khan Younis, Hamas said.
The Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed an 251 others taken hostage, triggered the most recent war in Gaza.
Since then, more than 74,650 people have been killed in the Palestinian territory, the health ministry there says.
Though a ceasefire was reached last October, Israel has continued occasional strikes it says are targeting remaining Hamas militants, which it argues it has the right to do under the terms of the ceasefire agreement.

Mia Latter was one of six women who made allegations against Brand in 2023
A woman who alleges that she was raped by Russell Brand when she was 16 has waived her right to anonymity and is campaigning for a staggered age of consent in an interview with the Sunday Times.
Mia Latter was one of six women who made allegations against Brand in 2023 as part of a Times, Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches investigation. She was known under the pseudonym 'Alice'. Brand denied the allegations at the time.
None of the women in the 2023 media investigation were complainants in Brand's recent criminal trial.
Reacting to the proposal, Cabinet Office Minister Louise Haigh said it would be a "massive step" to change the age of consent law, but that it "deserves proper consideration and scrutiny".
Speaking to the Sunday Times, she added that it was "disgusting" that a culture existed in the 2000s that "normalised and celebrated" celebrities having relationships with teenagers.
On Monday the entertainer was sentenced to 10 and a half years for one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He was acquitted of two counts of rape and one allegation of attempted indecent assault.
The Sunday Times reported that Latter had initially described the allegation about Brand to them as a sexual assault and that is how they reported it in their 2023 investigation.
Latter, 37, "now calls this allegation rape", the paper said.
Latter said she was 16 when she met Brand, who was 30 at the time, when she was on her way home from a shopping trip. She said Brand was working at MTV.
She told the paper: "I think people were so struck by my story because of the age difference and the clear imbalance [in power],"
She said Brand told her to keep their relationship secret from her school friends and claimed that he referred to her as "the child" in front of his entourage.
It was towards the end of their relationship that Latter was allegedly orally raped by Brand, according to the Sunday Times.
Latter said that she was now campaigning for the introduction of a "staggered" age of consent that would prohibit relationships between 16- and 17-year-olds and adults.
"I don't want to criminalise teenagers having sex with each other," she told the paper. "If you're between the ages of 16 and 18, it seems reasonable that you can have relationships with each other, and [teenagers] are always going to. But … if you're in your thirties, forties and fifties and you're trying to have a relationship with someone under the age of 18, it [should be] a criminal offence."
She also told the paper that she would not continue with the criminal process so she could focus on her campaign.
In her interview with the Sunday Times she said that the CPS decided not to include her as part of Brand's criminal trial but the police wanted her to be part of a "subsequent trial".
A Met Police spokesperson said: "Officers launched an investigation in January 2026 after receiving an allegation of rape.
"Detectives sought advice from the Crown Prosecution Service to determine how best to proceed, and officers were advised that further information was needed before a charging decision could be made.
"This investigation remains ongoing. We understand the delay has been distressing for this victim-survivor. However, our focus has been on putting forward the best possible evidence."
A spokesperson for the Crown Prosecution Service said it would "continue to work closely with investigators to provide advice and make sure cases progress as quickly as possible".

‘We think dialogue is a good thing,’ Australian PM says after German chancellor urges the US to work with Europe for peace in Ukraine
Australia has endorsed this week’s historic summit between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in China, even as European leaders warn that the US president must not make major concessions over the war in Ukraine.
The three-way summit is planned to take place in Shenzhen, where the leaders will gather for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) meeting. Likened to the 1945 summit at Yalta , the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, has warned the talks must not lead to a redistribution of influence among world powers or the abandonment of his country, more than four years into the war sparked by Putin’s full-scale invasion.
Speaking in Manila on Sunday, the Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese , welcomed the talks taking place but insisted the clear message to Putin was that the war should end.
Albanese, in the Philippines before a meeting of Quad leaders and talks with south-east Asian leaders at the Asean summit, left open the possibility of joining an Apec group photo with Putin if China wished for it to go ahead.
“We think that dialogue is a good thing and we await the outcome of that dialogue,” he said.
“It’s obviously quite significant, the fact that President Trump will be at Asean as well as at Apec, and that we’ll have a Quad leaders meeting as well.
“We want to see something constructive come out of that, including we want to see a de-escalation in the conflicts around the world.”
German’s chancellor, Friedrich Merz , expressed hesitation about the talks at a meeting of EU leaders on Friday.
“I want to state our message to the US very clearly once again: please, no surprises,” he said. “Stay on Team Europe and Team Ukraine , and let us work together for a genuine peace in Ukraine.”
France’s president, Emmanuel Macron , warned against forcing “an unjust peace” on Ukraine and, by extension, all of Europe.
“That is the spirit of defeat,” Macron said. “That is a recipe for another war.”
Zelensky has warned that the meeting must not turn into “Yalta 2, 3, 4”, invoking the conference in Crimea when the then US president, Franklin D Roosevelt, Britain’s Winston Churchill and the Soviet leader Joseph Stalin carved up influence across war-ravaged Europe.
The historian Timothy Garton Ash has called the trilateral summit, organised after a proposal by Putin last month, “a sort of parody” of Yalta, even as analysts say decisions on the future of Ukraine or China’s ambitions to take control of Taiwan without their involvement is unlikely.
Albanese said the summit would not undercut a growing push by countries including Australia and Canada for middle powers to have greater influence in world affairs.
“We’ll continue to engage with like-minded countries,” he said. “There are two super powers in the world.
“What’s important about the struggle of the people of Ukraine is that they’re not just standing up for their own sovereignty; they’re standing up for the international rule of law.”
Asked if he would join the so-called “family photo” of Apec leaders if Putin took part, Albanese said he would consider the wishes of China as the host nation. But he said the Russian president should know Australia’s opposition to the invasion.
“If he’s in a room where I am, I’m sure they’ll hear my contribution,” Albanese said.
After the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting, Australia’s Penny Wong joined with European and Canadian counterparts to avoid a group photo . It was cancelled by US officials when a third of participants declined to stand alongside the Russian foreign minister, Sergei Lavrov.
Albanese signed a new defence agreement with the Philippines on Sunday, visiting the supply ship HMAS Stalwart in the Port of Manila. Australia is helping to strengthen the Philippines’ defensive capability against Chinese aggression.
More freedom-of-navigation naval exercises are planned in an attempt to counter Beijing’s efforts to influence the South and East China seas.

These are two threat models for which disk encryption is the answer:
The device is stolen or lost and its contents must remain secret.
The device is tampered with, and all attempts at tampering must render it unusable.
Right now, we will focus on the first threat model. It is very difficult to build a tamper-proof system, and you need to worry about tamper-proofing your hardware, depending on what kind of actor is a realistic threat.
If we want to keep data on the system secret, we must first consider which data is worth protecting. On a NetBSD system, our data can be grouped into two broad categories:
Does the /bin/sh executable downloaded from the NetBSD FTP server contain any sensitive information?
On a BSD system, due to the separation of the base system and packages, many root file system directories are mostly unmodified outside of upgrades. In a properly configured system, nearly all system daemons and user applications are not going to be running as root , so won’t have permission to modify or create files in /bin .
We can reasonably assume that /bin/sh is the same binary that every other NetBSD user is running. A user may even opt to make directories containing such system files read-only.
The operating system needs to be able to load files to boot. [citation needed] This makes "true" full disk encryption difficult to achieve without specialized hardware, since the user needs some way to enter a password or an encryption key, and can’t do so without some form of software running on their computer. NetBSD also needs to store some amount of metadata about the encrypted partition on the disk, such as information on how to generate a secure 256-bit key from a 24 character password.
It is common for Unix systems to use shared libraries, which are loaded by programs to access system functionality. If these become unavailable, for example, by /usr/lib going missing, it becomes much harder to use the system. Familiarize yourself with the standard utilities in /rescue which don’t need working shared libraries to be useful.
The cryptographic algorithms that get standardized by the US government tend to be slow when implemented in software . This carries a performance penalty. As a result, many modern CPUs include implementations of ciphers like AES in hardware. For those that don’t, there’s alternative ciphers like Adiantum .
On a normal NetBSD system, several directories have a high chance of being modified during system operation:
/var - log files, system-wide databases (e.g. mail notifications), crash dumps…
/root - configuration files relevant to the root user account
/usr/pkg and /usr/local - where third-party software is installed
/etc - init scripts, system-wide configuration for the base system
A simple approach might be to encrypt /home . However, this might not be enough for some users. Although the crash directory can be easily changed with sysctl , a crash dump contains a snapshot of system memory which might be sensitive. If any servers have been run on the system, the log files might be sensitive. Mail sent to users (e.g. about their interrupted vi sessions and associated backups) might reveal sensitive file names.
Some users opt for the cgdroot approach, which uses only a small unencrypted ramdisk to pivot to an encrypted file system. However, this modifies the system startup routines significantly and may make certain rescue options harder. So, it’s worth asking whether there’s an approach that is somewhere in the middle, and still uses the standard NetBSD installation and boot process. Many BSD systems use separate file system partitions for /usr and /var , and this is a standard configuration supported by the NetBSD installer.
/etc is a harder problem to solve, since it contains files necessary to boot the system. However, on a typical desktop system, many files in /etc remain untouched. Passwords in /etc are generally stored only in hash form, except for Wi-Fi access points and certain VPN configurations (although it’s easy to reconfigure wpa_supplicant_flags to use a different configuration file from the default one in /etc ). Many configuration files are only loaded much later in the boot process, after /usr is already mounted, and can easily be replaced with symbolic links to files on another file system.
The NetBSD installer has basic functionality, but gets the job done quickly. In this configuration, we’re going to install NetBSD to a small unencrypted root file system. When you start to ignore the growth that can occur in /usr and /var and /home , even a complete NetBSD installation with development tools included is tiny. 4 GB should be more than enough.
For example purposes, I am going to use a sparc64 virtual machine, but the process is basically the same for more mainstream CPU architectures like amd64.
The installer detects that we already have a partitioned disk. We’re going to pick the "e: Delete everything" option so we have a fresh disk to start with:
Next, we’re going to choose "Set sizes of NetBSD partitions". This will allow us to have a small root, and reserve a large encrypted partition:
Here, I’ve decided I want a 4096 MB (4 GB) root file system, and a 11263 MB (11 GB) partition allocated for /var . Later, we’ll make /usr and /var share a disk partition, so don’t worry about this too much. Select "Go on".
On the next screen, I’ve changed the type of the secondary partition to "cgd" (listed under "Other type"), NetBSD’s encrypted device driver. I’ve also set its mount point to "-" so we can reconfigure it later:
I tell the installer I want to do a Full Installation and it completes as normal, installing everything into the small root partition.
When we reboot and log in as root , we enter a new world… our 4 GB unencrypted root partition.
Since I’m on sparc64, the disk is partitioned into disklabels. wd0 is the primary drive, and the disklabel command shows that /dev/wd0d is the partition reserved for our encrypted file system:
We can go directly ahead with creating a parameters file for the cgd :
Now cgd0 appears to the system as yet another disk, but all attempts to access that disk will be automatically encrypted/decrypted by the kernel.
The next time we enter our password, we want to be able to verify that the password was correct. This is done by choosing a verification method based on the contents of the encrypted partition. For flexibility’s sake, we’re going to put another disklabel inside the encrypted partition. This will allow the system to easily verify the password is correct by looking for a valid disklabel, but also gives us flexibility in our choice of file system.
This opens the interactive editor. We’re going to enter N to set a name for our disklabel (enter something like "cgdlabel"), then enter a to modify the first sub-partition.
First, it asks for a file system type. Enter ? to display a list of types:
Since I’m running -current and want to test the Log File System, I’m going to enter "4.4LFS". A more common and well-tested configuration would be "4.2BSD".
Since "a" is the only sub-partition at the moment, the default start of 0 is fine. "$" will use all available space on the cgd.
Finally, we’ll save our new label and quit the disklabel editor:
Now change the verify_method in /etc/cgd/wd0d to disklabel , and add a line in /etc/cgd/cgd.conf to create the cgd at boot time:
We can now access this hidden partition as /dev/cgd0a . But for it to be useful, we’ll need to create a file system on it. Once again, here I’m using the Log File System:
A more normal and well-tested configuration would be FFSv2ea:

Kış lastiği uygulaması ile ilgili sürücüleri yakından ilgilendiren bilgiler yer alıyor. Kış mevsimi yaklaştıkça, araç sahipleri için kış lastiği uygulamasıyla ilgili detaylar yeniden gündeme geliyor. Peki Kış lastiği uygulaması başladı mı, kış lastiği takmamanın cezası ne kadar ve hangi araçlara zorunlu?

Deputy prime minister says change would be a massive step but ‘deserves proper consideration and scrutiny’
The government has said it will consider calls to change the age of consent after a woman waived her right to anonymity to publicly claim she was raped by Russell Brand as a 16-year-old schoolgirl.
Mia Latter, now 37, alleged she had been orally raped by the jailed comedian when she was a teenager and he was 30 years old.
In an interview with the Sunday Times, she called for the introduction of a staggered age of consent – which would make relationships between adults and teenagers aged 16 and 17 illegal.
Louise Haigh, the de facto deputy prime minister, told the newspaper that Latter’s “heart-breaking story” meant a law change deserved consideration.
She said: “We need to listen to Mia and other victims like her who have been through these experiences because it’s really important that as lawmakers their experience is at the heart of what we consider.
“It clearly would be a massive step to change the age of consent, but it deserves proper consideration and scrutiny. I can absolutely understand why she is calling for it.”
Under UK law, adults of any age are legally able to have sex with 16 and 17-year-olds.
Latter said: “It’s shocking to me time and time again that whenever the news comes up again about him, it’s always in the comments about the relationship with a 16-year-old.
“That’s not the most heinous bit. But why is that the thing that everybody collectively gets stuck on? I think we all sort of agree that … adults shouldn’t be allowed to have sexual relationships with children, with somebody under the age of 18. That really doesn’t seem like a gigantic leap to take.”
Latter was referred to under the pseudonym of Alice in previous reporting by the Sunday Times, the Times, and Channel 4’s Dispatches documentary.
She was 16 when she first met Brand in Leicester Square, central London, while she was on her way home from a shopping trip.
He took her number and later messaged her, asking if she wanted to go for dinner, she said.
She told the newspaper that Brand – who was working at MTV at the time – still asked her to meet after she had confessed her age to him.
Latter alleges Brand orally raped her towards the end of their three-month relationship.
Brand denied all of the allegations made against him by Latter when they were first reported in 2023 by the Times.
She spoke to the police after the documentary, but the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) decided not to include her case in Brand’s trial at Southwark Crown Court.
He was convicted of attacks against four of the six women who gave evidence against him, and is now serving a 10-and-a-half-year prison term for one count of rape and three sexual assaults.
Earlier this week, it was announced that a series of “serious” sex offence allegations against comedian David Walliams are being probed by the Metropolitan police after an investigation by the Guardian and ITV News.
One woman described her alleged encounter with Walliams when she was 15 as “sexual assault”.
Haigh went on to say that, in light of news that one of Walliams’s accusers was asked to sign a non disclosure agreement (NDA), the government should also look at banning them in cases of alleged sexual assault and harassment. She said: “When we consider the allegations against David Walliams, teenagers who were fans wouldn’t come under the current consultation.
“I do think there is a very strong case to look at banning NDAs in all circumstances where they relate to harassment or discrimination, to make sure that no victim, regardless of where it happened or what their relationship was with the perpetrator, should ever be silenced.”
It is believed MPs outside Labour may support a bill to change the age of consent laws, with Jess Brown-Fuller, the Liberal Democrat justice spokesperson, coming out in favour of reviewing them.
Commending Latter for the “extraordinary bravery” it took to waive her anonymity, Brown-Fuller said: “I think we must go further to increase protections for young women and girls, and looking at a staggered age of consent is an important step.
“We already have rules that recognise power imbalances in professions: between teachers and students, or barristers and junior colleagues. It’s time for the government to recognise the implicit power imbalance held by older men over teenage girls.”
Latter’s decision to come forward was also praised by Bridget Phillipson, the minister for women and equalities, who said she “and thousands of others across the country will be in awe of her courage and determination”. She added that it is “up to all of us to send a message to women and girls who experience sexual violence: the shame is not yours. Women like Mia are leading the charge, but we can and must do more to make this a moment of change.”
Latter’s allegation was reported to the Met police, who said the investigation into the alleged rape remains ongoing.
A Met Police spokesperson said: “Officers launched an investigation in January 2026 after receiving an allegation of rape.
“Detectives sought advice from the Crown Prosecution Service to determine how best to proceed, and officers were advised that further information was needed before a charging decision could be made.
“This investigation remains ongoing. We understand the delay has been distressing for this victim-survivor. However, our focus has been on putting forward the best possible evidence.”
The CPS said: “The Crown Prosecution Service will continue to work closely with investigators to provide advice and make sure cases progress as quickly as possible.”

World Bank says India has pulled record numbers of citizens out of poverty, but millions among them are one shock away from being thrust back into destitution.
Rajsamand and New Delhi, India – Hema Prajapat, 25, says even “thorns growing inside her stomach” would not hurt as much as hunger does.
By the end of each month, her kitchen shelves are empty; her husband, Hari Prajapat, sinks deeper into debt; and an increasing share of their food supplies is set aside for their nine-year-old son, Divyansh.
She spends 11,000 rupees ($117) a month on her household of three. That is about 49 percent more than the roughly 7,380 rupees ($78) monthly threshold for a family of that size, based on the World Bank’s poverty line.
India, the world’s most populous country, no longer counts its poor. It has not published an official consumption-based poverty estimate in more than a decade. That leaves the World Bank to provide internationally comparable estimates, using newer consumption surveys and its own poverty thresholds.
A recent World Bank report says India lifted nearly 500 million people out of poverty between 2011 and 2023, with extreme poverty dropping from 27.1 percent to 2.6 percent during the period.
The only comparable poverty-reduction effort on this scale was achieved by China, which lifted more than 800 million people out of extreme poverty over four decades.
Several economists have said India’s achievement is significant, and that the World Bank’s mechanism for calculating these numbers is beyond reproach, even as they have argued that the planet’s most populous nation still has a long way to go before it can claim to have defeated poverty.
Other economists have questioned the World Bank’s sweeping conclusions and India’s unwillingness under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government to carry out its own poverty estimates.
But masked by that largely academic and political split is the lived reality of millions of Indians who have crossed the supposed poverty threshold yet lead a life marked by persistent deprivation, and a precarity that leaves families one shock away from losing everything that matters to them.
“This poverty line, this bar, is very low. No person can live a dignified life [on this amount],” Hema told Al Jazeera, sitting in a small garden where she moonlights as a caretaker.
“Did they even get out of their AC cars?” she asked, taking a dig at the officials who prepared the report for the World Bank.
India, home to 1.4 billion people, is one of the fastest-growing global economies – the fourth-largest by nominal gross domestic product (GDP), despite repeated recent shocks including the COVID-19 pandemic and the ongoing wars in Ukraine and the Middle East.
It is also one of the world’s most unequal countries, with the top 1 percent of its population owning 40 percent of its wealth – a concern highlighted in the World Bank report as well.
Hema was 11 when she was married off to a man who belongs to a family of traditional clay-pot makers in Rajsamand district of Rajasthan state.
When pot sales could no longer meet their financial needs, her husband, Hari, started a street food stall selling pani puri, a popular Indian snack. That did not last long because of the pandemic.
For the past year, she has been cleaning houses and washing utensils in the neighbourhood for 5,000 rupees ($53) a month, but the deprivation did not end.
“We have to buy every single thing from the market,” she said. The family has no agricultural land.
The World Bank pointed to rising female labour force participation as one of the factors behind India’s improving poverty rates, although women’s access to secure and adequately paid employment remains a challenge.
“Since I started working, our home has seen some comfort, but the money is now vanishing faster, and we are even more in debt,” Hema said, adding that she is unable to figure out the maths behind it.
“The prices have multiplied in recent years, and whatever we earn falls short,” she told Al Jazeera.
The World Bank also noted that the Indian government’s provision of free or subsidised foodgrains to nearly 800 million citizens every month under its national food-security programme has helped tackle extreme poverty.
But a rising cost of living has meant that government subsidies and handouts are racing against growing economic pressures on families like Hema’s. India’s overall consumer prices rose by at least 51 percent between September 2016 and September 2025, according to the government’s Consumer Price Index. Wage rises in this period have not kept pace.
Some government schemes help, such as public schools for children or state-run hospitals that provide free or subsidised healthcare.
But Hema says free healthcare does not inspire much confidence in people. When her son Divyansh had a bad cold and the flu two months ago, she rushed him to a private hospital as waiting times at public hospitals are often longer, with crowded wards, overstretched doctors and limited resources.
“I was scared for him. His fever was getting worse,” she said.
Treatment at the private hospital cost Hema about 6,000 rupees ($64) – more than what she makes in a month. “I do not want my son to get used to private hospitals or their drugs. I cannot take him to one every time,” she said.
Millions of Indian households that appear to be rising above the World Bank’s poverty threshold live on the edge, desperately trying to avoid being pushed back.
Santosh Mehrotra, a developmental economist in New Delhi, said the poverty threshold in India is too low. All it takes is “one shock” to be pushed back into it, he said. “That shock could be a pandemic, drought, flood, or even a wedding.”
In December last year, Salvi, 31, realised she was “finally pregnant” again – her second child after a gap of 14 years. Salvi did not trust government hospitals and wanted to get all her treatment at a private clinic.
In some ways, she had prepared for it. Over the previous eight years, she learned makeup skills and opened a small, one-seater salon in Kankroli, a small town in Rajsamand. She had been saving for her 14-year-old daughter’s higher education. The daughter currently goes to a government school.
“But when I got pregnant, I could not rely on government hospitals,” she said.
Maternal care cost her nearly 65,000 rupees ($695) and drained her savings. She had to pull her daughter out of extra tuition classes that cost her 600 rupees ($6) a month.
Mehrotra, who previously worked with the government on rural economies and poverty, said the World Bank’s poverty threshold is “also problematic because it does not draw a distinction between the rural and the urban populations” despite their different realities.
Seema Kumar, 37, lives on the outskirts of New Delhi and spends 20,000 rupees ($214) on her family of three.
She turns to loans when expenses spiral, such as during a festival or her 17-year-old son’s birthday.
As India celebrated Diwali, a festival of lights, last week, and people burst firecrackers, air quality in New Delhi – one of the world’s most polluted cities – hit a record.
The next morning, as dense and toxic smog hung over the city, all three members of Seema’s family left for work. By evening, her son had developed a sore throat, everyone in the family had a runny nose, and Seema went to bed with a terrible headache.
“I could not buy a mask for my son, and they say I am not poor any more,” Seema told Al Jazeera.
Back in Rajsamand, as Hema swept the garden in her neighbourhood, she called Hari, her husband, reminding him that their child was due for a routine medical checkup that day.
Hari said he could not afford to refill petrol any more due to the increase in oil prices caused by the conflict in the Middle East. Hema offered to refill his motorcycle’s tank to go to the nearest hospital.

Finishing negotiations for disputed South China Sea agreement will be a ‘tall order’, analysts say, amid China-Philippines tensions.
A long-awaited pact between the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and China for a “code of conduct” in the disputed South China Sea is unlikely to materialise during the regional bloc’s annual gathering of leaders in Manila this week, analysts and officials say.
The agreement would aim to manage tensions and prevent conflict at sea. But talks have dragged on for more than 20 years. In 2023, foreign ministers agreed to work towards finalising the accord within three years.
That deadline fell on 2026 – the year the Philippines took its turn as chair of ASEAN. Under its leadership, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) said negotiators have met at least once a month.
But they have fallen short of arriving at a consensus ahead of the summit.
“I just want to say that at this point in time, 80 percent of the document itself is finished,” DFA Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro said on Saturday, adding that there are some ‘salient’ points that still need to be ironed out.
She has previously said that geographical scope is one of the contentious issues. Beijing insists it has jurisdiction over nearly the entire South China Sea despite a 2016 international ruling invalidating that claim.
The Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei and Indonesia also have overlapping territorial claims.
The Philippines would also like the accord to respect the rights of countries outside the region, according to DFA spokesman Dominic Xavier Imperial. Half of the world’s merchant ships pass through the South China Sea.
But the country may be caught between a rock and a hard place.
“You can’t win it because if you get a good document, you’ll be accused of railroading or it would come across as self-serving. But if it’s a bad document, the Marcos Jr administration will be seen as a weak government,” Aries Arugay, a political scientist at the University of the Philippines, said.
China has consistently accused the United States and its allies, who regularly conduct freedom of navigation operations with the Philippines, of interference.
Tensions between Manila and Beijing have escalated since Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr took office in 2022. The China Coast Guard has repeatedly deployed water cannon against Philippine vessels and maritime confrontations have resulted in collisions and, on one occasion, a Filipino soldier losing a finger.
In recent weeks, the two countries have been engaged in a war of words.
In September, Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro’s public response to a handwritten note rejecting the 2016 South China Sea ruling – reportedly from Beijing’s military attache in Seoul – went viral.
“Perhaps basic decency and behaviour is what China needs to do,” Teodoro, who has been barred from entering China, said.
A month later, Beijing’s ambassador to Manila, Jing Quan, told reporters that if China wanted to use force, “we may easily win. But no, we will not choose force. We love peace”. The statement was made in response to a question about Teodoro calling China a “troublemaker”, but which Marcos said “sounded like a threat”.
What followed was a barrage of social media posts by Philippine officials criticising Jing, with the Chinese embassy replying in kind. Senators called for the expulsion of the Chinese envoy.
And, in late October, China accused Teodoro of a late invitation to the ASEAN defence ministers’ meeting in Cebu. Without ample time to prepare, it said it could only send its Manila-based defence attache.
“When that happened, I think the concern, especially on the part of the DFA, was, ‘We don’t want China not sending their premier. It would not look good on us as a host country,’” Lucio Pitlo, past president of the Philippine Association for Chinese Studies, said.
With just days before world leaders were due to arrive in Manila, diplomats from both sides stepped in.
In a phone call, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Lazaro, his Philippine counterpart, to rein in politicians.
“The Philippines should strengthen restraint over the relevant individuals and send a rational and unified voice on its policy toward China,” Wang said in a statement released by the Chinese embassy in Manila.
Lazaro described the conversation as having been “frank and constructive”.
However, the DFA followed up with a statement saying it found public commentary by certain government officials “regrettable”.
“Whatever personal convictions public officials may hold, their public platforms carry institutional responsibilities,” it said. “They may not pursue preferred approaches toward China, or any other international partner, without regard for the consequences on the government’s overall policy.”
Some analysts say the spat has further exposed division within the Marcos administration.
“They’re airing dirty laundry out there. It doesn’t communicate coherence. It doesn’t project a unified stance. This could have been an internal memo,” Arugay said.
But Pitlo said the last-ditch diplomatic effort had achieved its objective. Chinese Premier Li Qiang is now attending the ASEAN Leaders’ Summit in Manila.
Despite this, Pitlo shares pessimism about leaders reaching a conclusion to negotiations for a code of conduct in the South China Sea.
“I think with all the concerns about trade protectionism, the disruption in supply chains, economic issues will be very high in the agenda. I think it will be a tall order to get the code of conduct done.”

İnanır’ın hastalıkları sürecinde tedavi masrafları için bazı gayrimenkullerini sattığı iddia ediliyor.
Yeşilçam’ın usta oyuncusu Kadir İnanır, 26 Haziran’da 76 yaşında hayatını kaybetti. Vefatının ardından 23 yıllık hayat arkadaşı Jülide Kural ile ailesi arasında vasiyet ve mal varlığına ilişkin tartışmalar gündeme geldi.
İnanır’ın 9 Mayıs 2022’de doktor raporu eşliğinde hazırlattığı vasiyetinde tüm mal varlığını Jülide Kural’a bıraktığının ortaya çıkması, yeğeni Levent İnanır ile yaşanan anlaşmazlığı da alevlendirdi.
17 Aralık’ta açıklanması beklenen resmi vasiyet öncesinde aile üyeleri ile Kural arasında mal varlığı ve sanatçının özel koleksiyonlarıyla ilgili iddialar gündeme geldi. Bu süreçte usta oyuncunun banka kayıtlarında yer alan nakit varlığının 60 milyon TL olduğu öğrenildi.
Vasiyetinde de yer aldığı belirtilen 60 milyon TL dışında banka hesabında başka bir nakit varlığı bulunmadığı öne sürülen İnanır’ın, uzun yıllar devam eden hastalıkları nedeniyle yüksek tedavi masrafları yaptığı ifade ediliyor.
Usta oyuncunun özel hastanelerdeki tedavilerinin yanı sıra Küba’ya da tedavi amacıyla gittiği biliniyor.
2018’de beynine pıhtı atmadan önce akciğer kanseri süreci yaşayan İnanır’ın, bu dönemde Dalaman’daki yazlığını satarak tedavi masraflarını karşıladığı iddia ediliyor.
Daha sonraki hastalık süreçlerinde ise Ulus’taki evini sattığı öne sürülüyor. Yaşadığı Beykoz’daki evin de merhum iş insanı İsmet Acar tarafından hediye edildiği söylenmişti.
İnanır’ın vefatının hemen ardından yeğeni Levent İnanır ’ın, evdeki değerli eşyaların sayımı için polis eşliğinde eve girdiği belirtildi.
Ancak sanatçının saat, çakmak ve tespih gibi özel koleksiyonlarının kasada bulunmadığı iddiası da tutanaklara yansıdı.
Vasiyetten haberdar olan yeğenleri ve aile üyelerinin itirazlarının önemli bir bölümünün bu eşyalar ve mal varlığıyla ilgili olduğu konuşuluyor.
Banka kayıtlarında 60 milyon TL nakit varlığı bulunduğu belirtilen ve vasiyetiyle mal varlığını Jülide Kural ’a bıraktığı ifade edilen Kadir İnanır ’ın vasiyetinin resmen açıklanmasının ardından aile üyelerinin nasıl bir yol izleyeceği merak konusu.

Sabah saatlerinde köpeğini gezdirmeye çıkan Akalay, muhabirlerle ayak üstü sohbet etti. Akalay, “Her şey yolunda, birazcık hava alalım dedik ama size yakalandık” dedi.

Cape Verde goes to the polls on Sunday in an election that could see the African island nation appoint its first ever female leader. Justice Minister Joana Rosa challenges incumbent José Maria Neves, who is the country's fifth president since it became independent from Portugal in 1975.
Cape Verde could elect its first woman president Sunday as former Justice Minister Joana Rosa challenges incumbent José Maria Neves, who is seeking a second term.
Six candidates are competing, with a runoff scheduled for Nov. 29 if no candidate receives more than half the votes.
Rosa, backed by the opposition Movement for Democracy, is the first woman to run for president since independence from Portugal in 1975. Women have held senior cabinet posts, but Cape Verde has never had a female prime minister or president.
In Cape Verde’s parliamentary system, the prime minister directs government policy and holds most executive authority. The president’s role is largely symbolic, although the directly elected head of state can veto legislation.
The Atlantic island nation off West Africa , home to about half a million people, has a record of peaceful transfers of power and competitive elections in a region where that is rare. Nearly 77,000 Cape Verdeans abroad are registered to vote, almost a fifth of the total electorate.
Many voters feel distant from their leaders and want a president who understands their daily difficulties, while limited economic prospects were driving young people to seek opportunities abroad, said Roselma Évora, a professor of political science and gender studies at the University of Cabo Verde.
Neves, who won in 2021 with about 52% of the vote, has pledged to build cross-party support to improve housing, healthcare and education, create jobs and raise wages.
Incumbency gives Neves greater visibility, including among overseas voters, Évora said.

Rosa’s candidacy challenges traditional expectations of women’s roles in a society that remains “very patriarchal,” Évora said.
Rosa has centered her campaign on maintaining a balance of power, arguing that the country needs a counterweight to the African Party for the Independence of Cape Verde, which backs Neves and controls the government and most municipalities.
Known as PAICV, the party won a parliamentary majority in May, ending a decade of government led by the Movement for Democracy. A Rosa victory would again put the presidency and government in rival political camps.
Rosário Luz, a Cape Verde-based writer, said party loyalties mattered more than Rosa’s gender.
“We have a lot of women in politics, but we don’t have the policies for women that we should have,” she said.
Women carry much of the financial responsibility for their households in Cape Verde, but government policies have failed to address that burden, Luz said.

1963 yılında Necati Cumalı’nın Ege bölgesinin kırsal kesiminde yaşanan sorunları ele aldığı öyküsü Susuz Yaz, Türk sinemasının usta ismi Metin Erksan tarafından filme çekildi. Türk sinemasının ilk kez uluslararası ödüle layık görüldüğü Berlin Film Festivali’nde Altın Ayı kazanan eser, çocuk yaşlarındaki Hülya Koçiyiğit’in oynadığı ilk sinema filmi olarak da tarihe geçti.
Necati Cumalı’nın suyu odağına alan sarılarla bezeli öyküsünü beyaz perdenin unutulmazları arasına sokan Metin Erksan’ın aynı adlı eseri, İzmir’in Urla ilçesine bağlı Bademler köyünde yaşanan susuzluğu, Türk sinemasında star sistemini al aşağı ederek seyirciyle buluşturdu. Yeşilçam’ın aksine filmde daha önce hiç tanınmamış oyuncular rol aldı.
Aradan geçen 63 yılda küresel iklim değişikliğinin etkileri daha belirgin hale geldi. Su, artık ülkeler tarafından bir ‘milli güvenlik’ meselesi olarak algılanırken Susuz Yaz’ın kırılgan ve çaresiz Bahar’ı tüm gerçekliğiyle bu kez televizyon ekranında kendisini gösterdi.
63 yıl önce Bahar’a hayat veren Hülya Koçyiğit ile Kanal D’nin Ay Yapım imzalı yeni dizisi Susuz Yaz’da Bahar’ı canlandıran Lizge Cömert, dünyanın küresel ısınmaya çare aradığı bir zirvede buluştu. Birleşmiş Milletler (BM) İklim Değişikliği Konferansı COP31’de bir araya gelen iki kadın sanatçı, Metin Erksan imzalı Susuz Yaz’ın özel gösterimi ve söyleşisinde buluştu.
Etkinlik için Susuz Yaz’ın çekimlerinin devam ettiği Adana’dan Antalya’ya gelen Lizge Cömert, Hülya Koçyiğit ile birlikte “Susuz Yaz” afişinin önünde poz verdi. Usta oyuncu, Lizge Cömert’in elini tutarken “Hülya Koçyiğit el verdi.” diyerek halefine tam desteğini gösterdi.
Susuz Yaz’ın gerçek olaylardan esinlendiğini vurgulayan Hülya Koçyiğit, “İzmir Urla'daki Bademler Köyü'nde geçiyor. Gerçek karakterleri canlandırdık. Su bir kişinin olamaz, bunun hikayesiydi." dedi.
Koçyiğit, iklim değişikliğiyle mücadelede herkese sorumluluk düştüğünü söyleyerek, “İyi ki böyle bir organizasyon yapıldı. Çünkü dünyayı ne yazık ki çok hor kullandık. Ardı ardına felaketler yaşıyoruz. Bu, giderek dünyayı tükettiğimizi gösteriyor. " diye konuştu.
Susuz Yaz’ın Kanal D ekranında ‘yeni dizi’ olarak hayat bulacak olmasından duyduğu mutluluğu dile getiren Koçyiğit, “Kanal D'de yakında yayınlanmaya başlayacak Susuz Yaz dizisi beni çok heyecanlandırdı. Ben de baştan sona izleyeceğim. Merakla bekliyorum. " dedi.
Kanal D 'nin Ay Yapım imzalı yeni dizisi 'Susuz Yaz'da Bahar karakterine hayat veren Lizge Cömert ise usta oyuncuya duyduğu hayranlığı dile getirerek, “Ortak bir hikayeyi farklı şekilde yorumlayacağız. Çok heyecanlıyım." ifadelerini kullandı.
Senaryosunu Sema Ergenekon'un kaleme aldığı Ay Yapım imzalı Susuz Yaz dizisinin çekimleri Adana'da sürüyor. Hikayesi 1970'li yılların Çarlak Köyü'nde geçen yapımda Osman karakterini Mert Ramazan Demir, Bahar'ı Lizge Cömert ve Hasan'ı ise Batuhan Bozkurt Yüzgüleç canlandırıyor.

Sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı paylaşımda mutlu haberini duyuran 42 yaşındaki şarkıcı, paylaştığı karelere “Bizim minik prensesimiz geldi” notunu düştü. Lavigne bebeğinin ismini ve doğum tarihini açıklamazken, partnerinin ünlü biri olmadığı konuşuluyor.
Daha önce iki evlilik gerçekleştiren sanatçı; ilk evliliğini 2006-2009 yılları arasında meslektaşı Deryck Whibley ile, ikinci evliliğini ise 2013-2015 yıllarında Chad Kroeger ile yapmıştı.
Avril Lavigne (@avrillavigne)'in paylaştığı bir gönderi
Avril Lavigne, 27 Eylül 1984'te Kanada'da dünyaya geldi. Şarkıcı, söz yazarı ve oyuncu kimliğiyle tanınan Lavigne, müzik kariyerine genç yaşta adım attı. 16 yaşında Arista Records ile anlaşma imzalayan sanatçı, 2002 yılında yayımladığı ilk albümü Let Go ile uluslararası çapta tanındı. Albümde yer alan "Complicated" ve "Sk8er Boi" şarkılarıyla büyük çıkış yakalayan Lavigne, 2004'te Under My Skin, 2007'de ise The Best Damn Thing albümlerini müzikseverlerle buluşturdu. Her iki albümüyle Billboard 200 listesinde zirveye yerleşen sanatçı; "I'm With You", "My Happy Ending", "Nobody's Home", "Girlfriend" ve "Hot" gibi şarkılarıyla da müzik listelerinde başarı elde etti. 2011 yılında Goodbye Lullaby, 2013 yılında ise kendi adını taşıyan albümünü yayımlayan Lavigne, pop punk müziğin öne çıkan kadın sanatçıları arasında yer aldı.

Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday renewed his call for a national unity government with Gadi Eisenkot, who dismissed the appeal as a political ploy. This comes as the incoming premier is in the midst of negotiations to form a new administration.
Israel 's caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday reiterated his calls for a national unity government with his opponent Gadi Eisenkot , who in turn dismissed the appeal as a ruse.
The latest exchange comes as Eisenkot is in the midst of negotiations to form a government , after he was tapped for the post of premier on Sunday.
Read more Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as Eisenkot prepares government
A meeting with Eisenkot on Thursday "only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government" to guarantee Israel's security, Netanyahu said in a video statement, adding that such a government could "eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all".
He said this government would be made up of parties that recognise Israel "as a state for the Jewish people".
It would address security challenges, he added, most notably Iran which he claimed would "not hesitate to use nuclear weapons against us".
The outgoing prime minister warned against Eisenkot's plan to form a minority government, presented as a "national emergency government".
Such a plan would see the 48 lawmakers in Eisenkot's bloc vote in favour of his government, against the 46 Netanyahu backers. The 26 other members of parliament, from Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties, could abstain, allowing the government to be approved without an absolute majority in the Knesset , which has 120 seats.
"Instead of trying to form a weak and dangerous government... let's meet in one room, without preconditions, put aside all our disagreements and all the boycotts , and reach agreements for the security and the future of the state," Netanyahu urged.
Minutes later, Eisenkot responded by saying Netanyahu "knows he lost the election", accusing him of playing "tricks" by appealing for a unity government.
"Netanyahu is calling for negotiations while they are already underway; he claims to want unity but... sows division and stokes tensions as if there were no tomorrow," the former army chief said, adding that "these tricks don't work on me".
Eisenkot was tapped on Sunday to form a new government within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension.
Negotiations are expected to be difficult, especially as Netanyahu has waged a campaign to discredit Arab-Israeli parties, which gained a record number of seats in the election.
Netanyahu's proposed unity government would be made up of key Jewish parties ranging from the centre to the right, while excluding the Arab parties.
Read more Eisenkot pushes October 7 inquiry as Netanyahu targets Arab parties in tense new parliament
Eisenkot has indicated he would be open to forming a government with members of Netanyahu's Likud party, as well as outgoing Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich 's Religious Zionism, provided their commitment to unity is "sincere".
But a unity government with Netanyahu himself remains unlikely, particularly after Eisenkot denounced his "racist" campaign against Arab parties on Friday.
Eisenkot on Saturday reiterated his calls for a "break with the extremists", notably supporters of far-right minister Itamar Ben Gvir, as a condition for any participation in a government under his leadership.
Another point of contention is the election on Tuesday of the speaker of the Knesset, a post currently held by Amir Ohana, a close Netanyahu ally. The opposition has put forward Matan Kahana, a former officer in the Israeli army who was fifth on Gadi Eisenkot's list, to replace him.
"If they ( Likud and its allies) are truly seeking a sincere political partnership, as they claim, they must allow the democratic process to unfold normally... and instruct their members of parliament to support the appointment of Matan Kahana," Eisenkot said.

Gösterişli bir düğün yerine sade bir nikah törenini tercih eden çift, evliliklerini gözlerden uzak gerçekleştirdi. NR1 Magazin programına konuk olan Asena, "Kendi aramızda resmi nikahımızı kıydık" sözleriyle evlendiğini duyurdu.

Her şeyimiz, sütümüz, yoğurdumuz, peynirimiz oradan elde ediyoruz. Elimden geldiğince doğal olmayan hiçbir şeyi eve sokmamaya çalışıyorum. Erzurum'un Yakutiye ilçesi Pelit Meydanı'ndaki atölyelerinde yarma, çakım, nokta işçiliği, telkâri, oymacılık, gravür ve firuze-mercan sanatlarını bir araya getiren ustalar, tasarımına göre yapımı 4 gün ile 1 ay arasında değişen tespihler üretiyor. Fiyatları 50 bin ila 100 bin lira arasında olan tespihler, kimi zaman yapım aşamasındayken alıcı buluyor.
Tespihlerin işlenme sürecinde her bir tane üzerinde müşterinin talebine göre 500 ila 900 arasında delik açılıyor. Açılan delikler gümüş veya altın materyallerle tek tek doldurulurken, 33 taneden ve bir imameli bölümden oluşan tespihlerde on binlerce noktada ince işçilik gerçekleştiriliyor. Ustalar, farklı teknikleri bir arada kullanarak her bir tespihi tasarımına ve müşterinin isteğine göre hazırlıyor.
Tespihlerle 9 yaşından bu yana ilgilendiğini ve yaklaşık 24 yıldır bu alanda çalıştığını belirten 33 yaşındaki Cengizhan Çelik, farklı materyaller üzerinde çeşitli işleme tekniklerini uyguladıklarını ifade ederek, "Tespihin genel olarak yarma, çakım sanatı, firuze sanatı, işte ivory dediğimiz diş tespihler, Oltu taşı, kuka, hepsine gümüş işleme yapıyoruz. Genel olarak gümüş ve altın materyaller olmak başta olmak üzere fildişi, kuka, Oltu taşı, bu materyallere çalışıyoruz. Ortalama tespihin modeline göre bir hafta süren de var, bir ay süren de var, 4 gün süren de var. Biz her iki sanatın da aslında ortak temsilcisiyiz. Yarma sanatını da icra eden birçok ustamız, çakım sanatını da icra eden birçok ustamız var ama ikisini birleştiren şu anda Türkiye'de, hatta dünyada tek atölyeyiz, tek ekibiz. Yapım aşamasında attığımız videolar dâhilinde aynı gece giden ürün bile var daha bitmeden. Yani o gece giden de var. Bittikten sonra görüp o şekilde alanlar da var ama hemen gidiyor genellikle. Yani şöyle söyleyeyim, bunu Türkiye'de değil, dünyada uzaya çıkalım, farklı yaşam formlarını bulup, onlara soralım, şu anda bu iki sanatı aynı anda icra edebilen başka bir temsilci yok şu an" dedi.
17 yıldır tespih sektöründe çalıştığını belirten 30 yaşındaki Kadir Polat ise, "Şu anda da Cengizhan Çelik ile beraber çalışıyorum. Sanat çeşitliliğimiz birden fazla var. Sanat çeşitliliği sadece nokta işçiliği değil; nokta işçiliği, yarma işçiliği, telkâri sanatı, firuze, mercan sanatı, oymacılık, gravür işçiliği, birçok sanat çeşitliliğimiz mevcut. Ağırlıklı olarak şu an fildişi, yani ivory diye bilinen fildişi üzerinde işleme yapıyoruz. Yarma ve çakım işçiliği, telkâri işçiliği yapıyoruz. Onun dışında Oltu taşı ağırlıklı tespihlerimiz var, kuka tespihlerimiz var. Şu an sadece bu üç materyali çalışıyoruz. Gümüş olarak çalışıyoruz, gümüş ve altın olarak çalışıyoruz. Onun dışında materyal çalışmıyoruz şu anda. Şöyle birçok tespih yapım ustası tabii ki var, hepsi kıymetli bizler için ama şu an dediğiniz gibi bulunduğumuz ortam Türkiye'nin en kapsamlı sanat atölyesidir. Yani aynı anda bir ve birden fazla sanatın bir arada bulunduğu atölyedir. Yarma sanatı, telkâri sanatı, nokta sanatı ve bunun gibi birçok sanatın aynı anda döndüğü bir yerdeyiz şu anda ve birçok sanatı kendimiz icra ediyoruz. Baştan sona bütün aşamalarını kendimiz yapıyoruz" diye konuştu.

En son “Yıkılmayız Öyle” single’ını yayınladın. Şarkıda “Yıkılmayız öyle iki keder bir dertten” diyorsun. Seni ne yıkar, ne yıkamaz bu hayatta?
- Beni hiçbir şey yıkamaz. Çünkü hayat yıkılacak bir yer değil. Bir yıkılırsan, bunun ardı kesilmez. Hayat tabii ki inişli çıkışlı ama “Yıkıldım, bittim ben” diyeceğimiz bir noktaya gelmememiz gerekiyor. Bir şeyin beni yıkması çok zor ya...
- Küçük yaşlarda çok şey yaşadım. Babamın olayı olsun, annemin olayı olsun... O yüzden mi soğukkanlı oldum artık bilmiyorum. Hayatta her şeye hazırım. Sanırım istemeden soğukkanlı oldum.
Şarkıda baban İbrahim Tatlıses’in “Mutlu Ol Yeter” adlı eserinin müziğini kullanmışsın. Bu fikir nasıl çıktı ortaya?
- Mert Kemancı “Böyle bir şey yapsak mı?” dedi, hoşumuza gitti. İbrahim Bey’e selam çakmış olduk orada.
- Babamın çok büyük yorumları yoktur. Nokta atışı yapar ve gider. Öyle bir hengameye sokar ki, bu sefer çık işin içinden çıkabilirsen deriz. (Gülüyor)
- Çok büyük bir müzik adamı. Zaten İbrahim Tatlıses tek. Bir tane daha olması imkânsız. Kendi çocuğunun da onun gibi olmasını istiyor ama bu çok zor. Hem hayat olarak çok zor, hem onun yaşadığı şeyleri yaşamadığım için zor.
Onunla aynı düşüncede olmam. Çünkü o bir sürü şey atlatmış, bulunduğu yere gelmek için bir sürü şey yapmış. Bir sürü yoldan geçmiş. Çelmeler takılmış, hepsini aşmış, gelmiş. Şimdi aynı şeyleri benim yaşıyor olmam zaten zor. Kendisi gibi olmamı istiyor nokta atışlarla, hemen her şeyi çözmek için.
- Her ne kadar sahnede İbrahim Tatlıses şarkıları okusam da, ben daha pop yapıyorum. Onun sesi her şeye uyuyor. Ama onun yüzde 1’i kadar bende de olsun isterdim.
Single fotoğraflarında başka bir İdo var. Tarzın değişmiş. Seni takım elbiseyle görmeye alışkın değiliz...
- Aslında ben takım elbise seviyorum, çok da giyiyorum. Şortu bırakmak bana çok zor geldi. Çok zor koptum. Ama şort da bir yere kadar. Şimdi artık biraz daha normal giyime döndüm. Daha rahat, derli toplu hissediyorum bu arada. Konserlerimde artık orkestrayla sahneye çıkıyorum. Önceden mesela saçımı beyaza boyayabiliyordum. Çorapları eşofmanın üstüne çekebiliyordum.
Her şeyi farklı yapmayı seviyordum. Şimdiki madem şortu bıraktık, o zaman sahnemiz de değişsin dedik. DJ olmasın da daha büyük bir orkestrayla çıkalım diye düşündük. Kıyafet değişimimiz sahneye de yansıdı yani. Bambaşka bir şeye evrildik. Şortlu İdo gitti, bambaşka bir İdo geldi.
- Çok mutluyum. Çünkü bu işi birisinin çatısı altında yapmıyorum. Bir şirketim, bir patronum yok. İstediğim müziği yapıyorum, istediğim zaman yapıyorum. İstediğim şarkıyı çıkarıyorum, istemediğim şarkıyı çıkarmıyorum. Rahatım şu anda. Bu rahatlık bir tek müzikte var ama. O yüzden müzikte mutlu olduğum yerdeyim.
İbrahim Tatlıses’in oğlu olarak kendi müziğini ispatlamak seni zorladı mı?
- Hiç zorlamadı. “Sen” şarkım 300 milyon dinlendi. “Bileklerime Kadar Acıyor” ise 200 milyon... Bir sürü şarkı okudum, iyi tepkiler aldım. Bir tek şu zorladı beni; bazı insanların beklentisi farklı. İbrahim Tatlıses’in oğlu olduğum için “Senin takım elbise giyip halay çekmen lazım. Yakışmadı sana İdo” diyenler oldu. Ama benim hiçbir zaman onlara kendimi sevdirmek gibi bir derdim olmadı.
YouTube’da “İdo Show” programını yapmaya başladın. Yeni bölümler ne zaman gelecek?
- Kasım sonunda tekrar başlıyor. Kendimi çok mutlu hissettim orada. Çünkü sohbetimi canlı gören çok insan yoktu. Çok güzel de izlenmeler aldık.
- Var öyle bir düşüncemiz. Şimdilik YouTube’da biraz daha devam etmek istiyoruz. O platformda özgürce program yapmak cazip geliyor. Ama niye televizyonda da olmasın?
Seninle en son 2 yıl önce röportaj yapmıştık. O günden bu yana çocukların Emir ve Ayel büyüdü. Hayatının nasıl bir dönemindesin şu anda?
- Vallahi mükemmel geçiyor. Çocuklarla birlikte zaman algısı oluştu bende. 5-6 ay önce hiçbir şey konuşamayan çocuklar şimdi bayağı benimle iletişim kurabiliyor. Hayatımın en keyifli bölümündeyim.
Emir ile Ayel’in karakter özellikleri birbirine benziyor mu?
- Çok başkalar. Biri ketçap, biri mayonez. Biri tatlı, biri ekşi. Biri acı, biri acısız. Asla aynı değiller.
- İbrahim Ayel’in acayip bir özgüveni var. Ve bu beni çok korkutuyor. Her yerde dans eder. Eline bir tane mikrofon vereyim, dedesi gibi elini sallayarak bağırır. Onda bir şey görüyorum. Belki ikisi de ileride müzikle ilgilenir, belki de ilgilenmez. Bu konuda onları kısıtlayamam. Mutlu olacaklarsa yapsınlar. Ben o yaşlardayken babam işlerinden dolayı yanımda olamadı. Ama ben onlara zaman ayırabileceğim için müzikle uğraşmak isterseler ilgilenebileceğim. Bunu bildiğim için onlarla müzik yapma fikri çok güzel hissettiriyor.
Dedelerinin Türkiye’nin usta sanatçılarından biri olduğunun farkındalar mı?
Farkındalar. Ama mesela sahnede dedelerinin şarkısını okuduğum bir video izletiyorum onlara. “Kim bu?” diyorum, “Dede” diyorlar. “Babanız bu!” diyorum. (Gülüyor)
- Bence ben çok iyi bir babayım. Kendimi övmek için söylemiyorum ama vallahi çok iyi bir babayım. İlgiliyim. Onları yatırırım, kaldırırım, gece ağladıklarında yanlarına giderim. Hepsini yaparım yani.
İbrahim Tatlıses zaman zaman kardeşlerinle yaşadığı tartışmalarla gündeme geliyor. Ama sen bu konuda hep kendi kabuğunda kaldın, sessizliğini korudun. Senin düşüncelerin de merak ediliyor...
- Bir düşüncem yok aslında. Baba-çocuk arasında yaşanan şeyler. Benim bir şey söylemem saçma olur. Zaten benim neden bunu yaşadıklarına dair, ne olduğuna dair bir fikrim yoktu. Ben de televizyondan öğrendim. Çünkü bunları konuşmayı sevmem. Televizyonda konuşulmasını zaten sevmem. Ne kadar hatalı olursa olsun insan, bu abim de olsa derim ki “Abim, yapacak bir şey yok”. Babam da olsa “Babam, yapacak bir şey yok” derim yani. Ama bilmiyorum artık, hayat bir yerden sonra bazı şeyleri değiştiriyor. Ve değiştiği zaman da farklı şeyler olabiliyor. Ben hâlâ kendi kabuğumdayım yani. Kabuğumda kalmayı tercih ediyorum.
Seni rahatsız etmiyor mu bu tartışmalarla gündeme gelmeleri?
- Ediyor ama “Allah’ım ne olacak” dediğim bir durum yok. Çünkü öyle bir konu da yok gördüğüm kadarıyla. Kafama taktığım bir şey olmuyor.
- “Peri” diye bir şarkımız çıkıyor. Bir de Bilal Sonses’ten aldığım bir şarkı var. Onu da İlkay Şencan yapıyor. Yakında yayınlayacağız.
- İyi ki Yasemin’le evlenmişim. İyi ki iki tane çocuğumuz olmuş. İyi ki Emir’le Ayel olmuş. Şu an çok mutluyum hayatımda.
- Aramızda bazen konuşuyoruz. Yasemin kız çocuğu istiyor mesela. Çünkü giyinmeyi seviyor, fotoğraf çekmeyi seviyor, kremler, bakımlar falan... Bizim çocuklarla bunları yapamıyor. Onlarla bayağı güreşiyor, futbol oynuyor. “Bir de kız çocuğum olsa” diyor bazen. Hatta adını bile koymuş.
- İlk önce Mera, sonra Mevra dedi. Ben de dedim ki; “Yaseminciğim sen hastanede olacaksın, nüfus müdürlüğüne ben gideceğim”. (Gülüyor) Şaka bir yana, yeniden hamile kalırsa yine ikiz olma ihtimali var. Üstelik ikisi de yine erkek olabilir. Evde dört erkek çocukla Yasemin’e Allah sabırlar versin diyorum! Ama benim için mükemmel olur. Halı sahaya hep adam arıyoruz. (Gülüyor) Ben çocuğu çok seviyorum. O yüzden benim için hiçbir sıkıntı yok.

Şarkıcı İdo Tatlıses, babası İbrahim Tatlıses ile kardeşleri arasında zaman zaman kamuoyuna yansıyan anlaşmazlıklar hakkında konuştu. Hürriyet'e evinde röportaj veren Tatlıses, bu tartışmalarda taraf tutmadığını ve sessizliğini korumayı sürdürdüğünü söyledi.
Tatlıses, "Baba-çocuk arasında yaşanan şeyler. Benim bir şey söylemem saçma olur" dedi. Yaşananları kendisinin de televizyondan öğrendiğini anlatan şarkıcı, "Ben hâlâ kendi kabuğumdayım yani. Kabuğumda kalmayı tercih ediyorum" ifadelerini kullandı. Tartışmaların gündeme gelmesinin kendisini rahatsız ettiğini ancak kafasına takmadığını da ekledi.
Tatlıses, yeni single'ı "Yıkılmayız Öyle"de babasının "Mutlu Ol Yeter" adlı eserinin müziğini kullandığını hatırlattı ve bunu babasına bir selam olarak tanımladı. Şarkının sözlerinden yola çıkan soruya ise "Beni hiçbir şey yıkamaz. Çünkü hayat yıkılacak bir yer değil" yanıtını verdi.
Uzun süredir şort ve eşofmanla sahneye çıkan şarkıcı, tarzını da değiştirdi. Artık konserlerde takım elbise giydiğini ve DJ yerine orkestrayla sahne aldığını belirten Tatlıses, bu değişimi "Şortlu İdo gitti, bambaşka bir İdo geldi" sözleriyle özetledi.
Babasının müziğine de değinen Tatlıses, "İbrahim Tatlıses tek. Bir tane daha olması imkânsız" dedi. Kendisinin daha çok pop müzik yaptığını söyleyen şarkıcı, babasının yeteneğinin yüzde 1'ine sahip olmayı isteyeceğini dile getirdi.
Tatlıses, YouTube'da yayınlanan "İdo Show" programının yeni bölümlerinin kasım sonunda başlayacağını açıkladı. Şarkıcı ayrıca "Peri" adlı yeni şarkısını ve Bilal Sonses'ten aldığı bir şarkıyı yakında yayınlayacaklarını söyledi.
Haberler.com'da yer alan yorumlar, kullanıcıların kişisel görüşlerini yansıtır ve haberler.com'un editöryal politikası ile örtüşmeyebilir. Yorumların hukuki sorumluluğu tamamen yazarlarına aittir.

tv8'in Ocak ayında ekrana gelecek yeni dizisi Mükemmel Anneler’de kadro şekillenmeye başladı. Pem Yapım’ın ilk dizisi olan projenin iki kadın başrolü belli oldu ve iki isim de seyircinin yıllardır yakından tanıdığı iddialı oyuncular. Senaryosunu Sevgi Yılmaz’ın yazdığı, yönetmenliğini Koray Kerimoğlu’nun üstlendiği dizinin çekimleri Kasım sonunda başlıyor. Peki Neslihan ve Zümra karakterlerine kimler hayat verecek?
tv8'in yeni dizisi Mükemmel Anneler'in ilk güçlü imzası Deniz Çakır'dan geldi. Usta oyuncu, Mükemmel Anneler'de Neslihan karakterine hayat verecek.
Star TV 'de yayınlanan Çarpıntı, Ocak ayında beklenenden erken final yapmıştı. O günden bu yana yeni bir dizi projesinde yer almayan Deniz Çakır, böylece tam bir yıl sonra yeniden izleyicinin karşısına çıkacak.
Neslihan karakterinin hikâyesine dair henüz ayrıntı paylaşılmadı. Bilinen tek şey, dizinin kadınların dünyasını etkileyici bir dille anlatacak olması. Usta oyuncunun yeni rolü, Çarpıntı'daki performansını beğenen izleyiciler için de merakla beklenen bir dönüş anlamına geliyor.
Deniz Çakır'ın ardından Mükemmel Anneler'den ikinci kadro haberi de kısa sürede geldi. Ebru Özkan da projeye dahil oldu.
Ebru Özkan'ın canlandıracağı Zümra, Deniz Çakır'ın Neslihan'ıyla birlikte hikâyenin iki kadın başrolünden biri olarak öne çıkıyor.
Zümra'nın kim olduğu ve Neslihan'la nasıl bir bağı bulunacağı ise şimdilik gizli tutuluyor. Dizinin adı hikâyenin annelik etrafında şekilleneceğine dair ipucu verse de karakterlere dair resmi bir açıklama henüz yapılmadı. İki deneyimli ismin aynı projede buluşması, dizinin daha yayın tarihi kesinleşmeden dikkat çekmesini sağladı.
Mükemmel Anneler, dizi sektörünün tanıdık isimleri Efe İrvül ve Merve Girgin'in kurduğu Pem Yapım'ın ilk projesi. Yeni yapım şirketi, ilk adımını tv8 ekranlarında atacak. Pem Yapım'ın ilk dizisi için iki güçlü kadın oyuncuyu aynı hikâyede buluşturması da dikkat çekici bir ayrıntı olarak öne çıkıyor.
Dizinin senaryosu Sevgi Yılmaz'a ait. Yönetmen koltuğunda ise Koray Kerimoğlu oturuyor.
Çekimlerin ay sonunda başlaması planlanıyor. Her şey yolunda giderse Mükemmel Anneler, Ocak ayında tv8'de izleyiciyle buluşacak.
Öte yandan kadronun geri kalanı henüz açıklanmadı. İki kadın başrolün karşısında kimlerin yer alacağı ise merakla bekleniyor.
