England play their final Nations League group game in Madrid against Spain on Sunday; Three Lions will win Group A3 with victory over world champions; follow Spain vs England in our live blog on the Sky Sports website and App on Sunday, kick-off 7.45pm
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Thomas Tuchel insisted his words had been "twisted" as questions over anti-racism protocols overshadowed the build-up to England's Nations League showdown in Madrid.
Tuchel was asked after England's win over Croatia on Thursday how he and England would react if racist abuse occurred during Sunday's game against Spain.
The head coach responded by saying he would "maybe take five minutes" to remind his players of the anti-racism protocols. Tuchel also said "we will not expect" any abuse to occur in Madrid.
The game is England's first visit to the Spanish capital since 2004, when the match was marred by racist abuse directed at England's black players.
Spain were also fined and handed a partial stadium closure last month as punishment for Islamophobic chanting in Barcelona during a game against Egypt in March.
Luis de la Fuente was asked on Saturday by a Spanish-based English journalist: "Does the fact we keep talking about this topic demonstrate that Spanish football still has work to do in the fight against racism?"
In response, the Spain boss said: "What I can tell you, and you can pass this on to Thomas, is that there is no racism in Spain. That's how strongly I feel about it.
"There is no racism. Just as in England, there is no racism in Spain. None of us are racist."
Tuchel was then asked by a Spanish journalist about his counterpart's comments, to which he responded: "I was polite enough to ask [sic - answer] a question from your colleagues.
"And you run and ask the other coach, and tell him that I talk about racism in Spain. It's a perfect example of how it works.
"I never talked about racism in Spain. I answered politely a question about what happens. I never expect racism and the dressing room is the most anti-racist place on earth.
"You create a lot of confusion for absolutely nothing. It's a perfect example of how it should not work."
Tuchel then admitted he was "a little upset" by the situation, feeling he had been tricked to "create a lot of confusion for no reason."
When asked if he had a message ahead of the game to send to Spanish fans, he added: "I sent a message but it got twisted. I said I always expect a friendly atmosphere.
"I don't expect racism, nowhere. I am shocked if it happens. It should never happen.
"I am the first person to stand up for these values. I got asked what happens if it happens and I said there are protocols in place.
"Football does what it does best, brings people together - not divides."
England midfielder Declan Rice was also questioned on the topic, where he referenced previous incidents in which the national team had experienced racism.
Montenegro were charged by UEFA in 2019 for racist behaviour after former boss Gareth Southgate confirmed racist chanting was directed at Danny Rose during a 5-1 win.
The 6-0 win against Bulgaria in Sofia in the same year was also stopped on two occasions in the first half due to racist abuse directed at players.
Speaking ahead of facing Spain, Rice said: "In the past, I've experienced that in Montenegro, Bulgaria and there was a protocol in place we followed. We came off the pitch. We know exactly where we are as a group on that.
"The manager hasn't brought that up yet. It wouldn't surprise me if he brings that up tomorrow. But we know where we stand.
"I'm not expecting any of that tomorrow night. This is a beautiful city, great stadium, the players we're playing against we have a lot of respect for. It's set up to be a really good evening and hopefully not a negative one."

We are in the middle of the Second ReNESance (the first one is the one that saved the video game industry in North America). The combined decades of research and knowledge on how the venerable little NES works have produced a true cornucopia of games. We are all lucky to be here to witness it.
I am always happy to inform video game fans that the Nintendo Entertainment System is still receiving lots and lots of new third-party games.
In alphabetical order, because I refuse to rank them, here are 25 of my favourite modern NES games. Almost all can be obtained digitally, usually from the developer or publisher, most for a modest fee. Digital NES downloads are cheap! Most of these can also be obtained as physical cartridges for the true hi-fi experience on original hardware.
Made by 8-bit Slasher who has been honing his skills in other horror games for the NES, All Hell Unleashed is an extensive love letter to the horror slashers of the 1980s and 1990s. There is an underlying story about an evil cult that is trying to resurrect something or other, but that’s just an excuse plot so that you can fight Jaws, Freddy, Jason, Ghostface and others. It works surprisingly well. You can select your favourite horror movie from a stage-select screen to do your platforming as you fight the forces of evil, culminating in the boss fights where the villain of each horror franchise swoops in for a mano-a-mano . The platforming feels good, and the boss fights function as set pieces showcasing the real villains we are here to see in their 8-bit glory.
Finally Jason dons a better outfit on the NES than that silly purple jumpsuit!
After each classic horror villain is defeated, it is time to take on the cult itself for one final showdown. Definitely a spine-tingling adventure!
Alwa’s Awakening was originally a PC game made with pseudo-NES limitations (and in the case of the music, with actual NES limitations, as the developer used Famitracker to compose all of the music). If it doesn’t feel like a classic NES game and instead plays more like a modern indie Metroidvania, that’s because it is.
In the game, you play as Zoe, a girl who likes video games and one day awakens in the mystical land of Alwa, a place from one of her games. Your task is to guide Zoe through an adventure in Alwa where she will uncover power-ups that open up new avenues of adventure. Typical Metroidvania stuff, although a bit shorter than most games in the genre. The PC-to-NES port of this game was handled by my good friend Brad Smith of Lizard fame. He made a couple of interesting YouTube videos describing the process.
The game looks absolutely gorgeous for the NES, and its Famitracker-composed soundtrack made it through the porting process completely unscathed. There was a limited physical edition that today is only available via secondhand markets. If you can grab a copy, it’s a very high-quality production. This is some of the best stuff made for the system.
Anguna is an NES game with an interesting lineage. It was originally made in 2008 for the Game Boy Advance as essentially the same game, but a bit more to the standards of the GBA. Then it was successively ported to the Nintendo DS, the Atari 2600, and finally the NES.
The Atari 2600-to-NES port was done fairly faithfully, which means that the design decisions necessary for the Atari also made it into the NES port. This means, for example, no more than two enemies per screen and always of the same type. This sort of restriction isn’t unheard of in the NES, though. The very popular NES Double Dragon port also has the same limitation. The game design makes up for it and overall results in an enjoyable experience. And isn’t that what making and playing modern NES games is all about? An interesting experience made with strict hardware limitations.
So what is Anguna? At its most basic, it’s a Zelda-like. You walk around screens, you grab new tools, your tools open new paths for exploration, you use the tools to fight monsters, with the most common tool in question being your trusty sword. You are a nameless warrior who is notably NOT called “Anguna” on a quest to defeat the goblin king. Usual bare-bones plot.
Most might consider this game to be short, but I would say it’s sleek and streamlined. It doesn’t do much, but what it does it does well.
Oh, one very important upgrade that the game got during the 2600-to-NES conversion: rockin’ enemy portraits in gorgeous 8-bit pixel art!
Blazing Rangers is single-screen arcade firefighting co-op action! The firefighting genre is under-explored in video games and Blazing Rangers manages to represent it admirably.
The goal is to rescue the children in each burning level and proceed to the next one. To do this you have to snake a powerful firehose that can blast both flames and baddies as you make your way to the children. You may also and often must drop your firehose and rely on your backpack with water in order to get to the further reaches of each level. There are powerups to collect, which give bonuses such as increasing the length of the hose or activating a sprinkler system that will slow the spread of fire throughout the level.
You can control either of two characters, Popo and Mimi, each with slight differences in gameplay. Popo is a bit slower but can recharge his backpack with water faster while Mimi is the other way around. Each level is timed, but you’re more likely to be overrun by flames or enemies than running out of time. The children can get singed by the fire but otherwise seem unharmed, unless you get burned carrying them, in which case they get burned too.
The game has a very catchy theme song that is also the BGM of each level.
Although it can be fun enough in single player, co-op is where the game really excels. It is very fun to coordinate with your partner as there is still only one hose in co-op. A strategy, for example, could be to have one player get the hose extension powerup that the other player can instantly use to take the hose a bit further into the flames.
Estique is a horizontal shmup with the distinct honour of being made by some of the original Compile developers, veterans of the shmup genre. This is noticeable in that it even uses some sound effects from Compile classics such as The Guardian Legend . In the game you pilot the eponymous super-robot that can transform between the bipedal mecha form that can recover damage more quickly or a sleek spaceship form that is more manoeuvrable and has a faster firing rate. Gameplay consists of carefully balancing between the two forms in the heat of battle depending on whether a more offensive or defensive approach is needed at the time.
The NES manual has a deliberately awkward English translation as a homage to the quality of writing we often encountered during the licensed era. Accordingly, the Japanese and English versions of the game are not identical, with the English version having mild censorship of the cut scenes, mimicking the restrictions that Nintendo used to impose on licensed NES games.
The game’s default difficulty is a little on the easy side, and the whole game can be completed in under an hour at the default difficulty. I get the impression that the intended difficulty is a bit higher, so you can always adjust it up for your gaming needs.
Regardless of the difficulty, the giant screen-filling boss fights are always a delight.
Why 2nd adventure, you might ask? Well, this game has an interesting history . The original adventure was written way back in 2015 to support the Arc of Cowlitz County charity. Within a couple of years, a sequel appeared and physical copies were made and distributed at the Portland Retro Gaming Expo. They aren’t made anymore, but if you’re exceedingly lucky, you might be able to nab a second-hand copy somewhere. Finally the game was uploaded to itch.io as a free download, with a nudge to donate to the charity.
The game is a tightly-made single-screen arcade platformer where siblings Kaylee and J…

Antalya'da devam eden COP31 kapsamında düzenlenen söyleşide Susuz Yaz’ın dünden bugüne iki başrol oyuncusu bir araya geldi. Adana’da çekimleri devam eden Kanal D’nin Ay Yapım imzalı Susuz Yaz dizisinin Bahar’ı Lizge Cömert, Necati Cumalı’nın eserini usta yönetmen Metin Erksan’ın çektiği kült filmin başrolünde oynayan Hülya Koçyiğit ile buluştu. Etkinlikte iki başrol oyuncusu 1963 yılında beyaz perdeye yansıtılan ‘Susuz Yaz’ filmini konuştu.
Türk sinemasının unutulmaz yapımlarından, Metin Erksan'ın yönettiği 1963 yapımı 'Susuz Yaz', Antalya'da COP31 İklim Zirvesi kapsamında düzenlenen özel gösterimle yeniden sinemaseverlerle buluştu. Gösterimin ardından gerçekleştirilen söyleşiye katılan Hülya Koçyiğit, oyunculuğa başladığı yılları ve ilk filmi 'Susuz Yaz'ın hayatındaki yerini anlattı.
Henüz konservatuvar öğrencisiyken yönetmen Metin Erksan ile tanıştığını belirten Koçyiğit, “Ben oyuncu olmaya çok erken yaşta karar verdim. Konservatuvarda okurken kız kardeşim Metin Erksan ile film yapıyordu. Bir yaz tatilinde seti ziyarete gittim ve orada tanıştık. Yaşım çok küçüktü. Susuz Yaz'da Bahar gelini canlandırmama karar verildi. Ben kendimi hep tiyatro sahnesinde zannediyordum. Bu acemilik günlerimi atlatmam için köyde köylülerle yaşamamı istedi. Her gün sete gidiyordum ama çekimim olmuyordu. Köylü bir kız gibi hissetmemi beklediler" dedi.
Filmin gerçek olaylardan esinlendiğini vurgulayan Koçyiğit, “Hikayemiz gerçek olaylara dayanıyor. İzmir Urla'daki Bademler Köyü'nde geçiyor. Gerçek karakterleri canlandırdık. Su bir kişinin olamaz, bunun hikayesiydi" diye konuştu.
Koçyiğit, iklim değişikliğiyle mücadelede herkese sorumluluk düştüğünü söyledi. Koçyiğit, “İyi ki böyle bir organizasyon yapıldı. Çünkü dünyayı ne yazık ki çok hor kullandık. Kaynaklarımız tükenmeye başladı. Ardı ardına felaketler yaşıyoruz. Korkunç şeyler oluyor. Bu, giderek dünyayı tükettiğimizi gösteriyor. Biz de, madem bu dünya hepimizin evi, bize de çok görev düşüyor. En azından bu açıdan çok faydalı olduğunu düşünüyorum" dedi.
Söyleşinin ardından DHA'ya özel açıklamalarda bulunan Koçyiğit, 63 yıl sonra hikayenin Kanal D'de dizi olarak ekrana gelecek olmasından duyduğu mutluluğu dile getirerek, “Günümüzde Kanal D'de yakında yayınlanmaya başlayacak Susuz Yaz dizisi beni çok heyecanlandırdı. Ben de baştan sona izleyeceğim. Merakla bekliyorum. Eminim o da aynı özeni, aynı ihtimamı gösterecektir. Çünkü bilinmeyen bir hikayeden söz etmiyoruz. Bilinen, ünlü bir hikayeden söz ediyoruz" ifadelerini kullandı.
Filmin Türk sineması açısından taşıdığı öneme de değinen Hülya Koçyiğit, “Susuz Yaz, Metin Erksan'ın yönetmenliğinde Türk sinemasına uluslararası alanda ilk defa büyük bir ödül kazandırdı. Berlin Film Festivali'nde Altın Ayı Ödülü'nü kazandı ve sinemamızın gururu oldu. Benim de ilk filmim. Tekrar yepyeni bir neslin bu hikâyeyi izleyecek olması çok güzel bir şey. Dilerim hakkını verirler, dilerim başarılı olurlar" diye konuştu.
Hülya Koçyiğit, söyleşinin ardından Kanal D'nin Ay Yapım imzalı yeni dizisi 'Susuz Yaz'da Bahar karakterine hayat veren Lizge Cömert ile kuliste bir araya geldi. İki farklı kuşağın aynı hikayede buluştuğu görüşmede Koçyiğit, genç oyuncuya başarı dileklerini iletti. Yeni uyarlamanın izleyiciler tarafından merakla beklendiğini belirten Koçyiğit, “Filmi izleyen çok insan merak edecek ve izleyecek. Genç arkadaşlarımın görevi bize nazaran zor. Hep mukayese edilecekler. Başaracaklarına inanıyorum" dedi.
Usta oyuncuya duyduğu hayranlığı dile getiren Lizge Cömert ise “Ortak bir hikayeyi farklı şekilde yorumlayacağız. Çok heyecanlıyım, izledikten sonra düşüncenizi çok merak ediyorum" ifadelerini kullandı.
İki oyuncu, samimi sohbetin ardından birlikte hatıra fotoğrafı çektirdi.

texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cwp9:
An interactive reproduction of a self portrait by Kyffin Williams will allow visitors to feel the texture of the thick oil he used in his paintings
For the first time, the paintings of Sir Kyffin Williams have been brought to life in a new immersive experience at the National Library of Wales.
Technology similar to that used for exhibitions of Van Gogh, Cézanne and LS Lowry will immerse visitors in the mountain landscapes, hillfarms and stormy seas created by the painter, who is considered the defining Welsh artist of the 20th Century.
Images from Williams's oil paintings such as the hill farmer and sheepdog are animated in a 360-degree centrepiece and Sir Kyffin's life story is narrated by Sir Bryn Terfel in a bilingual presentation, with original paintings illuminated on the walls.
The National Library, which received grants of £500,000 to fund the project, said it hoped it will introduce a new audience to Sir Kyffin's work.
There are also interactive installations including a recreation of a self-portrait which can be touched, giving visitors a sense of the texture of Sir Kyffin's oil paintings.
He painted using an impasto technique - where paint is applied so thickly on to a canvas that it stands out in three dimensions.
Sir Kyffin, who was born on Anglesey in 1918, had a long relationship with the National Library, in Aberystwyth, Ceredigion, which has about 2,000 pieces of his work in its collection.
Moving images taken from Sir Kyffin's paintings are projected on to walls in what used to be an office in the national library
In 1950 the library bought its first two pieces from the young artist soon after he left the Slade School of Fine Art in London.
Morfudd Bevan, art curator at the National Library of Wales, said the library paid £15 for an oil painting of Cader Idris and £7.10 for an ink and wash drawing of Tre'r Ceiri on the Llŷn Peninsula.
Today, original work by Sir Kyffin sells for tens of thousands of pounds.
Bevan added: "The library saw the potential of this young artist.
"It was really important that we were encouraging and supporting young artists at the beginning of their careers, when Kyffin was trying to establish himself as a professional artist."
When he died in September 2006, he left a substantial part of his estate to the library, more than 1,200 works on paper, about 200 oil paintings, more than 300 original prints and his personal archive.
The national library holds the largest collection of Sir Kyffin's work in the world.
Morfudd Bevan said the national library has a long relationship with Sir Kyffin Williams - it bought two pieces from him for £22 at the start of his career
The library hopes the new attraction will introduce more people to his work.
Director of experience Carys Ifan said: "It's by no means a traditional exhibition.
"You go on a journey, literally moving through three rooms that used to be old offices. They've been repurposed because we are so keen to open up more and more to the public."
Profiad Kyffin Experience was made possible by technology invented by Focal Studios, an immersive experience company and the main designers of the exhibition.
Chief executive Dennis Outten said working on the project had been a "labour of love" and an "incredible journey for everyone involved".
In the first room Sir Bryn Terfel tells the story of Sir Kyffin's life in a biligual narration while images taken from his work are projected on to the walls
Focal Studios worked with another company, leo&hyde, to animate Sir Kyffin's paintings in a 360-degree immersive experience so they come alive in projections on the walls and floor.
"It's like you're in one of his paintings, I love it," Outten said.
"It's not like virtual reality, because you can hold the hand of your child, you can sit there with your grandmother or your friend and you experience it together. I think that's incredibly powerful."
Inside the "projection cave", visitors see scenes painted by Sir Kyffin come alive as the cattle, waterfalls, the farmer and his sheepdog move around them.
Outten said high fidelity scans of Sir Kyffin's original work and creative techniques helped bring the paintings to life.
"We actually created a 3D model of Kyffin's farmer and dog, and then using animation techniques, puppeteering them essentially to move."
Rhodri Llwyd Morgan, the library's chief executive, said the new experience was part of a strategy "to be more popular, more appealing and that's our aim".
The experience was formally launched on Thursday and opens to the public from 18 November

texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cm78:
Shane MacGowan was best known as the frontman of The Pogues, a band that injected rural folk songs with the punk spirit of the 1970s
On the day of Shane MacGowan's funeral , his heartbroken wife found comfort in the same thing that moved and captivated the rest of the world that afternoon - the music that filled a parish church in Nenagh, County Tipperary.
Mundy and Camille O'Sullivan performed Haunted. Nick Cave sang A Rainy Night in Soho. And Glen Hansard and Lisa O'Neil led mourners in a send-off rendition of Fairytale of New York .
"I thought, well, if we just got all the people who were at the funeral on a record, that'd be something pretty special," Victoria Mary Clarke told BBC News NI.
On Friday, three years after her husband's death, that idea came to fruition with the release of 20th Century Paddy.
"It must be wonderful for Shane... I think up in heaven, he's very aware of what's going on," said Clarke.
There are 36 tracks on the new album - all penned by MacGowan - and 40 bands and soloists.
Among those are contributions from two acclaimed Irish artists who have passed away since recording their covers for the album.
Glen Hansard is featured performing Bottle of Smoke, while Moya Brennan provides her interpretation of Mother Mo Chroi.
"I feel love and connection between the artists (on the album) and Shane.
"And also, you know, for me personally, it feels like a lot of love because when somebody sends something nice to Shane, they're sending it to me."
The Pogues frontman died aged 65 at his Dublin home in 2023, following a hospital stay after being diagnosed with encephalitis.
Shane MacGowan and Victoria Mary married in 2018 after several decades as a couple
Victoria was too fair to say who delivered her favourite cover on the album, but she was frank about how she personally benefited from the project.
"It gave me so much pleasure and it gave me so much joy and hope for the future to work on it because it gave me something to do every single day for three years and it got me out of bed and it got me to make new friends."
In the aftermath of her husband's death, that "social life and a sense of purpose" was invaluable to her.
But while the album is certainly bound up with MacGowan's death, it's not overshadowed by it.
"I think the artwork, if I had to pick, might be my favourite thing about the album," she chirped, an artist herself.
Bruce Springsteen spent time with Shane MacGowan at his home before his death
The term a 'who's who' doesn't quite capture the calibre and genre-defying diversity of the line-up featured on 20th Century Paddy.
There are hall-of-famers like Bruce Springsteen and Tom Waits.
Iconic, generation-crossing indie bands like The Jesus and Mary Chain and The Libertines.
And for anyone who needs reminding of how far above its weight Ireland punches when it comes to music, have a look at the back of 20th Century Paddy.
U2, Hozier and Bob Geldof - people with permanent residencies at top of the music industry.
There are stalwarts and custodians of the Irish folk tradition, Damien Dempsey perhaps foremost among them.
And lots of other artists, less established but very much in their ascendancy - Amble, Kingfishr and Madra Salach, to name but a few.
David Keenan said Shane MacGowan serves as an example of the importance of authenticity in art
David Keenan, a singer-songwriter from Dundalk, whose thoughtful lyrics and intense live performances are invoke something of MacGowan himself, told BBC News NI he was honoured to be asked to add to the album.
"Fairytale of New York is as old as Christmas for me," said David.
But his epiphany moment came when an uncle gave him The Pogues' third album.
At 11 years old, Keenan said If I Should Fall from Grace with God "lit a flame" inside him.
"That (album) was the first time I heard all these references to mythology and drink and rebellion and, you know, heartache.
"It gave me permission as a kid to get stuck into real lyric writing. And to do it in the traditional and folk form."
On 20th Century Paddy, Keenan covered Sick Bed of Cúchulainn - a celtic punk ballad from their 1985 album Rum Sodomy and the Lash, the central allusion of which is the mythical Irish warrior Cúchulainn.
This has real significance for Keenan, who as a child in Louth, used to play near the standing stone (Clochafarmore) where Cuchulainn was said to have been killed.
He did his recording of the song in Drumlish, County Longford, where he said "Shane used to record too".
"It was just was surreal and at the same time perfect, you know."
Before putting his version down on tape, Keenan did something few artists would have done: he recited a poem he had written in Irish asking permission from MacGowan to sing the song.
"I felt connected to Shane's energy during the recording, you know."
Keenan said the quality of the artists on 20th Century Paddy showed the "global respect that was there for Shane's abilities, you know, as a lyric writer, a poet".
He added that, at a time when there is "a lot of pressure on young musicians now to go viral on TikTok and dumb themselves down... here's an artist who didn't do that".
"In an age of ChatGPT and generative AI", said Keenan, MacGowan is a reminder for "human beings to be authentic".
Keenan's top picks from the album included Summer in Siam covered by Tom Waits, Jimmy Artache's version of USA, Glenn Hansard's Bottle of Smoke and Steve Earle's If I Should Fall From Grace With God.
But, given the quality on the album, the list, he said, could have gone on... and on... and on.

China is forced to tread carefully as it considers hosting a meeting between Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin, and Donald Trump. While the optics are sure to favor Moscow, Beijing is risking its image on the global stage.
An unprecedented meeting between the leaders of China , Russia and the United States could be happening on the sidelines of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China's tech hub of Shenzhen this week.
China has yet to confirm that the meeting will take place. However, a Chinese Foreign Ministry official recently told the press that Beijing was "in communication" with relevant parties. In Moscow, a Kremlin representative said work on "coordination" was underway.
The clearest indication about the potential summit came from US President Donald Trump last weekend. Talking to reporters at a Florida airport, Trump said he "thinks" one of the meetings planned for APEC will be with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping .
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Despite the lack of official confirmation from either Beijing, Moscow, or Washington, the media has already dubbed the potential trilateral summit a "new Yalta," invoking the optics of the US, UK, and Soviet Union convening at the end of World War II and deciding on the new geopolitical power balance in the Crimean resort town.
At the same time, nobody seems to be quite sure what the three leaders would talk about if China agrees to host the trilateral summit at APEC.
In his brief remarks to reporters on Sunday, Trump avoided mentioning Russia's war in Ukraine when asked about the possibility of the meeting, bringing up only "Iran" and "denuclearization" as possible talking points.
The Chinese Foreign Ministry reported "no information" when questioned earlier this week about the potential substance of talks.
A three-way meeting with a photo op would be a big diplomatic win for Russia's President Putin. Since launching the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, the Kremlin chief has faced years of diplomatic boycott by Kyiv's allies , most notably the US under Trump's predecessor Joe Biden.
Putin first pitched the idea of a trilateral summit last month during a call with Trump . The Wall Street Journal has reported that Putin wanted the meeting to discuss an end to his war in Ukraine.
For the US, the president standing shoulder to shoulder with the leaders of America's foremost rivals could be a bad look, although Trump has already made a show of personally greeting both leaders with a red carpet at different points during his second term.
As host, China is in an even trickier position. While Russia and China are broadly aligned on many issues , Beijing does not want to be explicitly tied to Russia's war in Ukraine and harm China's efforts to present itself as a long-term force for global stability .
The Chinese government is also working to rebalance economic ties with the EU. The European powers would likely bristle at a summit hosted by China and discussing the war in Ukraine without Kyiv or Brussels present at the table.
"China is clearly uneasy about the possible trilateral meeting with the US and Russia, and although Beijing has shifted its position from saying nothing to admitting that the three powers are in contact, the vagueness of these declarations seems deliberate," Alicja Bachulska, Asia policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations (ECFR), told DW.
"Beijing is aware of the potential negative optics of the 'Yalta 2.0' framing, even if this historical comparison is inaccurate and does not reflect current geopolitical dynamics," Bachulska said.
She notes the trilateral meeting could "trigger further escalation in the already worsening relations between China and the EU" if Ukraine is discussed with no Europeans in the room.
For China, there is also little to gain in terms of optics. Images of Xi standing with Trump, the leader of Beijing's top rival, and Putin, Beijing's partner in opposing the US, could present an awkward look.
"Even if the meeting only yields a photo opportunity, it could nevertheless severely erode China's image," Bachulska added.
Putin and Xi have met some 40 times since the Chinese president came to power in 2012.
The two neighboring countries have grown especially close following the declaration of "no limits" partnership accord in early 2022. The move was announced by Xi and Putin on the sidelines of Beijing Winter Olympics, just weeks before the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
The current Russia-China ties are deeper than they have been in decades.
At the core of the axis between the two nations is a long-term strategy to contain US power while fostering an alternative global order both Moscow and Beijing can use for their own ends.
Throughout the course of the Ukraine war, which is nearing the end of its fifth year with no solution in sight, Beijing has quietly provided Russia with crucial market for energy exports, while supplying technology and so-called "dual-use" goods.
While China did not explicitly provide Russia with weapons, its exports included high-tech components that could be used for modern weapons systems like drones.
Officially, Beijing maintains neutrality on the Ukraine war and has refused to take responsibility for its outcome .
"China is more interested in reforming global governance in ways that reflect its preferences and red lines while preserving a collegial appearance," Aurelio Insisa, senior analyst at the Berlin-based Mercator Institute for China Studies (MERICS), told DW.
Even if China agrees to host the meeting, it will likely avoid framing it as three top powers making decisions for the rest of the world, according to Insisa.
"Embracing the 'G3' narrative would undermine its image as a champion of the Global South and developing countries. It is also worth noting that Beijing has shown no interest in engaging with the one pressing issue that could realistically be addressed in such a trilateral format: nuclear disarmament," he added.
In a report published in August, the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission (USCC), painted China as a "decisive enabler" of Russia's war in Ukraine.
Beijing was "converting Moscow's dependence into lasting military, technological, economic, and geopolitical advantages while avoiding the obligations of a formal alliance," according to the US body.
However, the commission also noted there were limits to Beijing's strategic support, and intelligence and security concerns remain a constraint on deeper cooperation. The report emphasizes the relationship is more of a strategic alignment than an alliance, with deep mistrust remaining in some key areas.
Russian defense firms, for instance, have accused Chinese companies of stealing intellectual property. Beijing, on the other hand, is concerned with Russia's growing strategic relationship with North Korea , which has reduced Pyongyang's dependence on China.
China and Russia also differ on nuclear doctrine. While Beijing maintains a longstanding "no first use" policy, Moscow uses nuclear threats as part of its strategy.
MERICS' analyst Insisa believes the cooperation between Russia and China will largely continue within this year's framework, including Russia providing energy and potentially transfering military technology in the "few remaining areas where it retains an advantage."
"China, in turn, will continue to supply dual-use technologies, purchase Russian energy, provide Moscow with a measure of diplomatic cover, and — more importantly — offer channels for circumventing Western sanctions," he added.
Notably, China will also get a "privileged vantage point" on how the battlefield in Ukraine is evolving land warfare.
"Strategic distrust between the two sides, particularly Russia's concerns about economic dependence on China, will continue to limit the scope of their cooperation," Insisa said.

Holly Humberstone says she was having an identity crisis on a weekly basis
You might know her as a pop star, endorsed by everyone from Taylor Swift to Sam Fender, but Holly Humberstone has a secret double life.
In her spare time, the singer-songwriter is literally a cat burglar.
"We've stolen one of our neighbours' cats by accident," she laughs, in a Zoom call from her fixer-upper in New Cross, south-east London.
"He's a tiny little black cat who's come into our garden and simply chosen us."
Under the slightest scrutiny, however, her story crumbles like a biscuit in a hot cup of tea.
"OK, we've been coercing him into the house with treats," she admits. "He's just so cute.
"But we're not trying to keep him. We literally push him out every night."
Humberstone's excuse for this feline felony is that, last year, her parents sold her childhood home in Lincolnshire , external and moved to Wales – taking her pets with them.
One, a cat called Tsuki, had even been immortalised in the song Lucy as a confidante who listens to her problems but "never judges".
"Oh, she knows some secrets!" laughs the singer. "I'm so glad she can't talk."
"We actually tried to bring her to London with us, but she's a countryside cat and she hated it so much. We had to send her to Wales where she can be free and frolic."
Her parents' relocation was disruptive for the human Humberstones, too.
Their house, a "freezing cold, falling down" property 20 minutes outside of Grantham, played a huge part in the singer's success.
Her early EPs were all written there, inspiring the "wonky sonics" of her indie-leaning pop sound. The 2021 single Haunted House is even dedicated to the "friendly" spirits who inhabited the property.
"It's a place I always felt I could go back to, to remind myself of who I am," she says.
Instead, she spent 2025 "packing up 23 years of stuff my family and I had accumulated", from her old ballet shoes and poetry books to forgotten bits of jewellery.
The singer shared photos of her old bedroom, and the artefacts she'd rediscovered, while clearing out her parents' "haunted house" in Grantham (pictured, left).
The process was unsettling. Already grappling with the idea of leaving childhood behind, Humberstone found herself literally throwing away her past.
"I felt uprooted. I was having some sort of identity crisis almost weekly," she says.
So she did what she's always done, and poured those feelings into her second album, Cruel World, which entered the UK charts at number four earlier this year.
"Writing these songs felt like building myself a little shield and a kind of safety bubble," she says. "There's an escapist, fantasy element to so much of the album."
Maybe that's true, but Humberstone has always had the ability to locate a song's emotional core, and the lyrics on Cruel World don't disappoint.
" To lose somebody is to know you're only human, honey, " she sings on To Love Somebody , external , soothing her elder sister as she endures an agonising break-up.
Undeterred by that heartbreak, she throws herself headfirst into a new affair on Die Happy , external , declaring: " Hit the gas, I want it fast, want it reckless ."
But the most revealing song is the closing track, Beauty Pageant , external .
Fragile and raw, it's the sound of Humberstone in her dressing room, addressing the woman in the mirror who'd "die for the applause" but who struggles with the impossible beauty standards imposed on female artists.
Humberstone's biggest songs include Falling Asleep At The Wheel, The Walls Are Way Too Thin, Die Happy and Scarlett
"That's a song that I wasn't really setting out to write," she confesses.
"Writing about other people often feels easier than turning the magnifying glass on yourself."
The lyrics, she says, draw on a "very specific" mindset she acquired at her all-girls school in Grantham.
"It was drilled into me: You're all in competition. You're only rewarded if you're the best. And if you're not, you're worthless."
The experience "really warped the way I view other girls", she says.
Musical success made it worse. After winning the Brits Rising Star award in 2022 , Humberstone found herself competing with megastars, even though her music leaned towards the alternative side of pop.
"I'm a very small fish and I recognise that, but suddenly I was in meetings being compared to all these people on my label's roster, who are on a completely different scale," she says.
"It's something I really, really struggled with in the early days and it's something I've really had to unlearn."
Nowadays, Humberstone has stopped benchmarking herself against her peers, recognising that the need for validation never fades.
"I don't think that there's a point I could get to, or an award that I could win, where these feelings would disappear," she says.
"Everybody feels like they've still got something to prove, so I'm done with setting myself goals - because then I lose sight of the real reason that I'm doing this, which is to write music that represents me, and have other people feel understood through that music."
"I pray that one day I'll turn and face the mirror with a smile," sings Humberstone
That mindset comes to fruition in the new, expanded edition of Cruel World, whose five new songs were largely written after the original album was handed in.
"I was super proud of Cruel World and, when you've got that in your back pocket, there's room to experiment and break some of your usual parameters."
The new tracks find Humberstone embracing a new persona – more confident, more flirtatious, a little salty – with music inspired by a playlist featuring Abba, Madonna and Robyn.
The single Too Cute To Be Lonely , external is a will-they/won't-they story set at a house party.
" Don't leave a girl upset, in such a pretty dress ," she teases the object of her affections.
Terminally Yours takes place a couple of weeks later, when Humberstone realises she's fallen head-over-heels in love.
" Your stupid face is my sorry fate ," she harrumphs, cross at herself. " For [expletive]'s sake, I'm in love ."
Silver Sky, a gorgeous acoustic ballad, tells another side of the story, as she settles into her lover's arms and drifts into blissful reverie.
"I wrote that on a kind of Hail Mary trip, seeing what fell out of the air in Nashville," she reveals.
"We went over to [co-writer Maddie Diaz's] house, took a guitar into the garden and wrote Silver Sky outside, while all of these gorgeous red cardinals were singing around us.
"I usually write a lot about my mental health struggles, but I was just in the mood to write something that made me feel good."
Humberstone won the Brits Rising Star award in 2022, joining the ranks of former winners such as Sam Fender, Florence + The Machine and Adele
Not that her mental health issues are in the rear view mirror. Humberstone admits her stage nerves have only intensified since the release of Cruel World.
"It's the proudest I've been of any of my work and, for that reason, I struggled with shows because I felt a lot of pressure to go out and deliver it to the standard that I think people are expecting.
"But on the other hand, it's totally fine if you mess up or sing a wrong note. People can't connect to a pop star that feels too robotic and polished.
"So maybe my strength is that vulnerability, and I need to recognise that more."
That vulnerability has won Humberstone millions of fans, even if a hit single has (so far) eluded her.
And her audience keeps growing. In May this year, her breakout single Falling Asleep At The Wheel was awarded a silver disc... five years after its release, indicating that her songs have staying power in an era of disposable hits.
Astonishingly, this is news to Humberstone, who learns about the accolade during our interview. But it helps to clarify a thought that's been knocking around her head.
"If I'm going to be doing this for years to come, I've just got to keep making music that feels right, trusting my gut and realising there's no en…

ABD 'de hava trafik kontrol merkezlerini etkileyen iletişim arızası nedeniyle ülke genelinde 4 saatten fazla durdurulan uçuşlar yeniden başladı. Operasyonlar toparlanırken iptaller ve gecikmeler sürüyor, çok sayıda yolcu havalimanlarında mahsur kaldı. Yetkililer hava ulaşımının pazar günü mesai bitimine kadar tamamen normale dönmesini bekliyor.
ABD Ulaştırma Bakanı Sean Duffy, Federal Havacılık İdaresinin (FAA) 13 Kasım'da aldığı uçuşları durdurma kararı sırasında havada bulunan 3.500 uçağın güvenli şekilde iniş yaptığını açıkladı. Cuma günü için planlanan yaklaşık 50 bin uçuşun 30 bini, durdurma kararı alındığında tamamlanmış veya havadaydı. Kalan seferlerden 8 bini gerçekleştirilebilirken yaklaşık 12 bin uçuş yapılamadı. Bunların 9 bininin ticari uçuş olduğu bildirildi.
Basın toplantısı düzenleyen Duffy, sistemin yeniden tam kapasiteyle çalışmaya başladığını belirterek aksaklığın yalnızca eski donanımlardan kaynaklanmadığını, telekomünikasyon altyapısının da güncelliğini yitirdiğini söyledi. Rutin bakım çalışmaları sırasında eski bakır kablolar üzerinden hizmet veren hatlar fiber optik altyapıya dönüştürülüyordu. Arızanın yönlendirici ekipmandan mı yoksa yüklenici firmanın çalışmalarından mı kaynaklandığı henüz belli değil. Duffy, olayın siber saldırıdan kaynaklandığına dair bir bulgu bulunmadığını ve sistemlerin yürütülen çalışmaların izole edilmesinin ardından yeniden devreye girdiğini kaydetti. FAA Yöneticisi Bryan Bedford ise uçuşları durdurma kararının, istikrarsızlığın nedenleri araştırılırken hava sahasındaki yoğunluğu ve operasyonel baskıyı azaltmak için alındığını bildirdi.
Sistem yeniden çalışmaya başlamasına rağmen hava yolu şirketlerinin operasyonlarını toparlaması zaman alıyor. Uçakların ve mürettebatın yeniden doğru noktalara ulaştırılması sefer programlarının oluşturulmasını zorlaştırıyor. Bedford, cumartesi günü planlanan 41 bin uçuşun yaklaşık 4 ila 5 bininin iptal edilmesinin beklendiğini açıkladı. FlightAware verilerine göre Türkiye saatiyle 20.00 itibarıyla ABD genelinde 4 binden fazla uçuş iptal edilirken 3 binden fazla seferde gecikme yaşandı. Hava yolu şirketlerinden alınan bilgilere göre uçuş programlarının pazar günü mesai bitimine kadar tamamen normale dönmesi öngörülüyor.
Yaşanan kriz, ABD 'nin hava trafik kontrol altyapısındaki teknolojik eksiklikleri yeniden gündeme taşıdı. Duffy, kontrol merkezleri ve iletişim sistemlerinin modernize edilmesi gerektiğini vurgulayarak Kongre'den hava trafik kontrol sisteminin yenilenmesi için 50 milyar dolarlık kaynak ayrılmasını istedi. Mevcut sistemlerin günümüzün ihtiyaçlarını karşılamakta yetersiz kaldığını söyleyen Duffy, altyapı yatırımlarının daha fazla ertelenmemesi gerektiğini belirtti.

texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/art:
Having been unbeaten in Craig Bellamy's first nine games, Wales have only won four of their past 16 matches
It can be easy to get tangled up in the complexities of Nations League permutations and, although Wales still have a few uncertainties to iron out, the picture is becoming clearer for Craig Bellamy's side.
Following their 3-1 defeat in Norway on Saturday, Wales will finish bottom of Group A4 even if they win their final game against reigning champions Portugal on Tuesday.
But that does not mean they will definitely be relegated from the top tier.
Instead, they are almost certain to play one of the teams from League B in a relegation play-off in March.
However, one thing is for sure: As a result of the Norway loss, Wales will not be among the top seeds for Euro 2028 qualifying.
"We wanted to be in pot one. That was the drive," said head coach Bellamy after the defeat in Oslo.
"Some people might say, 'what makes you think you should be in pot one?' But I do.
"Maybe I'm naïve. I see in big parts of that game we can be in pot one. Let's take the good bits from the game, definitely improve on certain moments of the game and just keep pushing."
A point against Portugal would make sure of it, but even if they lose, Wales will most likely end up in a relegation play-off.
Only the two worst-performing sides will be automatically relegated to League B.
With one game left, the other bottom teams in League A - Turkey, the Czech Republic and Serbia - all have no points, whereas Wales have three.
For them to finish among the worst two, they would need to lose to Portugal, and two of the other teams would need to win their final fixture with a significant swing in goal difference.
Wales have a goal difference of -5. Considering Turkey (-10) visit France, Czech Republic (-10) are in Croatia and Serbia (-7) travel to Greece, it would require an unlikely turn of events for Bellamy's men to be automatically relegated.
Wales have conceded eight goals during this Nations League campaign
The relegation play-offs will be held across two legs at the end of March, with the first leg between March 25-27, and the second between March 28-30.
As a League A side, Wales will be seeded and therefore play at home in the second leg.
The draw for the play-offs takes place at Uefa's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland, on Friday, 20 November.
The sides that finish in the top two of League A's four groups will also discover the quarter-final draw on the same day.
Slovenia, Northern Ireland, Kosovo and Bosnia-Herzegovina are currently all in second place in their groups.
However, Scotland, Ukraine, Austria, the Republic of Ireland and Poland could also be potential opponents.
Wales have scored three goals in five games during this Nations League campaign
All teams finishing third or higher in League A will be named as top seeds for Euro 2028 qualifying.
By missing out, Wales could now be drawn alongside one of Europe's heavyweights in their group.
Spain, France, Italy, Netherlands and Portugal are among the sides already guaranteed pot one seeding for the draw on 6 December in Belfast.
England will also be a top seed, although Thomas Tuchel's men will be kept apart from Wales and the other Euro 2028 co-hosts in qualifying regardless.
When it comes to reaching the Euros, the 12 group winners and eight best-ranked runners-up qualify directly.
For any of the co-hosts who don't make it via that route, there are two automatic spots available. Those will be awarded to the best-ranked between the four nations who haven't qualified directly.
If Wales still haven't made it, there is still the back-up option of the play-offs.
And given play-off places are based on Nations League rankings, Wales are highly likely to already have that safety net.

Modern sanat tarihinde monokrom, resmin temsilden, anlatıdan ve renk çeşitliliğinden uzaklaşarak kendi maddi ve kavramsal sınırlarına yöneldiği önemli bir kırılma noktası olarak öne çıkıyor. Kazimir Maleviç’in Siyah Kare ’si tek renkli yüzeyiyle resim için yeni bir başlangıç alanı açarken, Aleksandr Rodçenko’nun kırmızı, sarı ve mavi monokrom çalışmaları bu yaklaşımı resmin sınırlarına kadar taşıyor. Böylece monokrom, yalnızca bir renk tercihi olmaktan çıkarak resmin ne olduğu ve hangi unsurlardan arınarak varlığını sürdürebileceği üzerine bir sorgulamaya dönüşüyor.
İsmail Şimşek’in Monokrom sergisi ise bu tarihsel mirası farklı bir perspektiften ele alıyor. Sanatçının son dönem çalışmalarından oluşan sergi, modernizmin tek renkle arınma idealini tersine çevirerek renkli ve katmanlı yüzeylerin altında devam eden değişmezliğe işaret ediyor. Şimşek’in pratiğinde monokrom, tek bir rengin saflığından çok, farklı renklerin ve malzemelerin bir araya geldiği yüzeylerde değişmeden kalan yapısal bir durumu ifade ediyor. Bu yaklaşımda renk, yalnızca canlılığın göstergesi değil; görünüş ile görünüşün altında varlığını sürdüren gerçeklik arasındaki mesafeyi açığa çıkaran bir unsur olarak beliriyor.
Heykel eğitiminin kazandırdığı yapısal düşünme biçimi, Şimşek’in malzemeyle kurduğu ilişkinin temelini oluşturuyor. Sanatçının yüzeyleri, Piet Mondrian’ın resimsel düzen anlayışı ile Naum Gabo’nun konstrüktif mekân yaklaşımını bir araya getirerek çizgi ve rengin maddesel bir yapıya dönüştüğü alanlar yaratıyor. Mondrian’da çizgi, renk alanlarını birbirinden ayırarak kompozisyonun düzenini kurarken Gabo’nun çalışmalarında mekânsal ilişkileri ve kuvvetin yönünü görünür kılan yapısal bir öğe olarak karşımıza çıkıyor. Şimşek ise bu iki yaklaşım arasında kurduğu ilişkide çizgiyi yalnızca sınır belirleyen bir işaret olmaktan çıkarıyor. İpler ve düğümler aracılığıyla çizgi, yüzeyi hem bölen hem de parçaları birbirine bağlayan fiziksel bir unsura dönüşüyor.
Sanatçının çalışmalarında renk de benzer biçimde, yüzeye eklenen optik bir değer olmanın ötesine geçerek formun oluşumuna doğrudan katılan maddi bir niteliğe bürünüyor. Tek renkli zeminler; ipler, kumaşlar ve dar dokumalar aracılığıyla bölünüyor, geriliyor, sarılıyor ve yeniden birbirine bağlanıyor. Bu müdahaleler, yüzeyde bir yandan düzen oluştururken diğer yandan sürekli hissedilen bir gerilim yaratıyor. Böylece çizgi, temsil eden bir işaretten maddi bir kuvvet hattına; renk ise görsel bir nitelikten yapının taşıyıcı unsurlarından birine dönüşüyor. Resimsel alan ile heykelsi yapı arasındaki sınırda şekillenen bu kompozisyonlarda denge, tamamlanmış ve kalıcı bir uyumdan ziyade her an değişebilecek kırılgan bir ilişki olarak varlığını sürdürüyor.
Şimşek’in renkli olmak ile renkli görünmek arasında kurduğu ayrım da serginin temel meselelerinden birini oluşturuyor. Yüzeydeki renk çeşitliliği ilk bakışta canlı ve uyumlu bir bütünlük izlenimi yaratsa da bu görünümün altında malzemenin, çizginin ve yapının taşıdığı gerilim varlığını koruyor. Sanatçının ifadesiyle denge, “henüz ayarı bozulmamış bir ‘şu an’” olarak tanımlanıyor. Bu geçici an, eserlerdeki biçimsel ilişkilerin sürekli yeniden kurulduğu, uyum ile bozulma ihtimalinin yan yana var olduğu bir alan açıyor.
İsmail Şimşek’in Monokrom başlıklı kişisel sergisi, 26 Aralık 2026 tarihine kadar SANATORIUM Tophane’de ziyaret edilebilir.

Portugal were hammered 4-1 by Denmark on Saturday, an embarrassing Nations League defeat in their first match without Cristiano Ronaldo after his retirement from international football.
Rasmus Højlund starred with a superb double as Denmark moved into second place in Group A4 and closed in on a spot in the quarter-finals with an exceptional display in Braga.
Denmark are on nine points from five fixtures, three behind Portugal who were already sure of qualification for the last eight having won all four of their previous group fixtures.
A draw against third-placed Norway on Tuesday will see Denmark through.
Before kick-off Portugal paid tribute to Ronaldo, who announced his exit from the international game last week, with the team and mascots walking out wearing Ronaldo’s No 7 and his name on their jerseys.
Denmark were the better team from the first minute and it was no surprise when the visitors took the lead from Pierre-Emile Højbjerg’s penalty in the 43rd minute.
Højlund lashed home a volley four minutes after the restart and seven minutes later the home crowd were stunned after the Napoli striker skipped past Rúben Dias before crashing home a powerful shot from the edge of the area.
Boos and whistles began to ring out at the Estadio Municipal when Joachim Andersen headed in the fourth, and Bernardo Silva’s late consolation effort barely dampened the discontent.
Wales suffered a 3-1 defeat to Norway in Oslo to dent their hopes of staying in the top tier of the Nations League .
Antonio Nusa and Andreas Schjelderup struck in the space of nine second-half minutes as Norway turned the screw. Substitute David Brooks halved the deficit 11 minutes from time as Wales finished strongly.
However, Connor Roberts brought down Schjelderup and Erling Haaland converted from the penalty spot, extending his Nations League goals record to 23, as Norway avenged their October defeat in Cardiff.
It means Wales will definitely finish bottom of Group A4, irrespective of Tuesday’s result at home to Portugal.
Although they could finish on six points with Norway, they have a worse head-to-head record and could now face a playoff in March to avoid relegation to Group B.
Terry Devlin’s first international goal kept Northern Ireland top of their Nations League group as a 1-0 win over Ukraine set up a promotion decider away to Hungary on Tuesday.
The 23-year-old Devlin has been in the goals for Portsmouth this term with four, and opened his Northern Ireland account with a fine strike in the 68th minute as he left the Ukraine goalkeeper Anatoliy Trubin flat-footed with a shot from distance.
Pierce Charles then made a superb save to deny Danylo Sikan and preserve Northern Ireland’s fifth consecutive clean sheet – the first time they have achieved that since 2017 – and ensure they remain the only side in the competition yet to concede.
The victory put Northern Ireland back on top of Group B2 after Hungary’s 2-0 win over Georgia earlier in the afternoon, and ruled Ukraine out of contention as they lost three successive matches for the first time in six years.
A draw in Budapest would be enough to elevate Michael O’Neill’s team to League A, while even in defeat they would face a playoff in March, and they have also earned a pot two place in next month’s Euro 2028 draw.
However, O’Neill will need to watch Tuesday’s match from the stands as he joined Jamie Donley – who had a first-half strike ruled out for offside – in earning a late yellow card that results in a suspension.
Sasa Kalajdzic dealt the Republic of Ireland a late blow in Linz with the only goal in Austria’s 1-0 victory at the Raiffeisen Arena.
The result ensured that, no matter how the closing contests in Group B play out, Austria sealed promotion to League A. Ireland enter Tuesday’s critical home match at the Aviva Stadium in third place, with one point fewer than their final opponents, Kosovo.
Heimir Hallgrímsson’s team were not without chances, but only Kalajdzic made one count when the former Wolves striker poked home from close range in the 79th minute.

Today, England have the chance to finish top of their Nations League group if they can beat the world champions Spain. If Spain’s 3-2 victory over England in September is anything to go by, we’re in for a treat this evening. Defensive errors ultimately cost England in that game so they will need to be almost flawless to end Spain’s 43-match unbeaten run.
Elsewhere, Chelsea beat Manchester City 1-0 in the Women’s Super League yesterday to go top of the table. There are three more WSL games this afternoon, including Arsenal v London City Lionesses.

Hallgrimsson's side sit third in Group B3 before their final game
Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson says their 1-0 defeat by Austria in their penultimate Nations League game was "painful".
Substitute Sasa Kalajdzic poked home the winner in Linz, with the narrow victory ensuring Austria claimed top spot and automatic promotion to League A.
Chiedozie Ogbene squandered a late chance to equalise for the Republic and Hallgrimsson was frustrated they left the Raiffeisen Arena empty-handed when they had chances to secure the win which would have kept their hopes of winning the group alive.
"It was painful not to get anything from this match. I think we deserved at least a draw, but we needed the win for this game to count," he told RTE.
"I think we had the chances, the openings and the positions to do that, but this was not our day in goalscoring, so it is disappointing.
"Everything that we asked the players to do, they did and I think they gave everything.
"For that reason, we should be happy in a way but, obviously, we don't want to be building something, we want to win games."
Saturday's defeat left Hallgrimsson's side third in Group B3, a point behind Kosovo, who they face in their final game in Dublin on Tuesday.
Hallgrimsson was left to rue Republic of Ireland's inability to clear the corner from which Kalajdzic scored.
"We actually did have a lot of chances from that second ball in the box but it kind of never fell for our players in a good position," he added.
"They have a corner that they score from on the second or third touch. That's the game at this level. You need to be switched on and focused every second of the game."
Picking up a second win in the group against Kosovo would secure second place in the group which brings with it a promotion play-off and a move up to pot two for next month's Euro 2028 qualifying draw.
The Irish fell to a 1-0 defeat in Pristina in September and Hallgrimsson needs his side to finish strongly at home and pick up a vital three points.
"It was always that [Kosovo] game that was more important, but we were just so close to winning this one and being able to win the group but this is football at this level, it is all down to details."

Match report from the UEFA Nations League Group A4 match between Norway and Wales at Ullevaal Stadion; Norway won 3-1 thanks to goals from Antonio Nusa, Andreas Schjelderup and Erling Haaland; Wales now bottom of Group A4 as threat of relegation grows
Wales suffered a 3-1 defeat to Norway in Oslo despite a spirited performance, as the threat of relegation to the second tier of the Nations League now looms over Craig Bellamy's side.
Wales looked the better side in the first half and had chances to take the lead, most notably through Daniel James on three occasions, before they unravelled after half-time.
Antonio Nusa showed why he is often referred to as the Norwegian Neymar as he broke the deadlock with his fine strike into the bottom left corner before substitute Andreas Schjelderup tapped home Erling Haaland's pass to give the hosts a commanding lead.
David Brooks' sublime chipped finish sparked hopes of a comeback but Haaland's penalty, after Connor Roberts pushed Schjelderup down in the box, punctured the late momentum they had gathered.
Wales are now guaranteed to finish bottom of Group A4 with a worse head-to-head record against Denmark and Norway - the two teams they could have potentially drawn level with on six points by beating Portugal in their final group game in Cardiff.
A draw against Portugal on Tuesday would guarantee Wales a Nations League relegation play-off in March against a League B runner-up.
Wales knew finishing in the top three of their Nations League group would see them join Europe's heavyweights in pot one at next month's Euros draw in Belfast.
"We wanted to be in pot one. That was the drive," Wales boss Bellamy said of missing out on top seed status in Euro 2028 qualifying.
"Some people might say, 'What makes you think you should be in pot one?'. But I do.
"Maybe I'm naive. I see in big parts of that game today that we can be in pot one.
"Let's take the good bits from the game, definitely improve on certain moments of the game and just keep pushing."
Wales will be Euro 2028 co-hosts alongside England, Scotland and the Republic of Ireland - and actually get the tournament under way in Cardiff should they qualify.
"There is loads for us to improve on but I've liked a lot of it, I have to be honest.
"It's not that we want to sit in, we always look at the pressure on the ball and I thought at times first half we did that really well.
"When we tried to trigger, we were able to move the ball well, and then turn into attack for us even from deep areas.
"So it was a lot of good things, but in the second half I just felt we lost a bit of momentum. We lost a bit of energy and that was a difficult period."
Wales were energised by their substitutions as Bournemouth forward Brooks and Cardiff playmaker Rubin Colwill brought new life to the attack.
Bellamy said: "I thought Rubin and Broosky were top and 'Sparky' (Mark Harris) brought the energy and the intensity he's going to give you.
"I thought the subs really gave us that push again and we got it to 2-1.
"But we made a mistake and it falls to a player who was offside, but then he isn't offside by the time he hits the ball."
"A reminder Wales have Portugal in their final group game on Tuesday.
"Even a win won't be enough to get off bottom spot due to head-to-head records with Denmark and Norway.
"They will avoid automatic relegation to tier B, though, if they don't finish as one of the two worst bottom-placed sides in tier A.
"Wales are on three points, with the other bottom sides in tier A currently on 0 points.
"A relegation play-off against a side from tier B would be the alternative."

The former England centre-back answers your questions on Diego Maradona, Bobby Robson and on staying in strange places
“H ave you made up all these on your own?” asks Terry Butcher, sitting in a London office in the week he is presented with his England legacy cap. It turns out dozens of Guardian readers want to pick the brains of a much-loved centre-back who was feted en route to a World Cup semi-final and tormented four years previously by the mercurial genius of Diego Maradona.
Did Maradona ever admit to the “Hand of God”? Butcher found himself in the post-match doping-control room alongside his nemesis at the Azteca in 1986. “I tapped my head, then my hand, and then he tapped his head,” Butcher says. “He didn’t admit to it because, if he had, I’d have been right across that room.”
The highs and lows of Sir Bobby Robson’s remarkable England tenure are chronicled in a new book co-written by Butcher: Almost Immortal: When Bobby Robson’s England Gripped The Nation.
Your name instantly brings to mind you playing on for England with a bandaged head and bloodied shirt. With hindsight, should you have left the pitch? Sian Williams
I never contemplated leaving the pitch at all. As the captain of your country, playing in a crucial World Cup qualifier against the top team in our league, in our group, there’s no way. I said to Bobby: “If you take me off, I’ll hit you.” I don’t think I would have but I said: “No, don’t do it!” Initially, I felt the blood and it seemed like a bad one, quite severe, but when I was bandaged up I could still play and it wasn’t a problem. Heading the ball wasn’t an issue because you’re really fired up, the adrenaline’s there, so it didn’t concern me. There was no way I was going to voluntarily come off unless Bobby was of a mind to do that, but he knew my pain threshold very well and knew I would battle on. I had numerous injuries before, broke my nose in 1982, five weeks in hospital and lost a lot of blood. So he knew I had great fortitude. Things have changed dramatically now. From a medical point of view it would have been right to take me off, absolutely. But that was then and I think, as a captain, you have to lead. It’s nice that people remember me through that image, but I was just doing my job.
I once stayed at the hotel that forms part of the FA’s headquarters at St George’s Park. Above the bed, and hanging over my wife and me all night long, was a giant version of the photo of you covered in blood. It was a bit disconcerting – but what’s the strangest place you stayed in or visited while on England duty? Stu Egan
I’ve actually stayed in that room as well. Stu has told us what it was like for him and I have to say it wasn’t great for me either. I’m staring up looking at me with a bloodied head and thinking: “Oh my God, this has followed me around.” At least when you close your eyes and sleep you don’t have to see it, but I’m sorry he had to stay there.
I didn’t stay in many really strange places with England. When I was manager of Motherwell we had a Scottish Cup quarter-final and were in administration at the time. I was organising our travel myself and booked a hotel near Stranraer, online. It looked great, right by a golf course. But when we got there we realised it was a residential home for the elderly. The rooms had accessibility handles and low sinks. It wasn’t a horrible place at all, quite the opposite, it was very warm and caring. But it was strange coming down for breakfast seeing people being looked after by the nurses. We won 4-0 so it can’t have been bad for us.
Now that time has passed and Diego has left us, has your perspective on that afternoon in Mexico City softened at all, or do you feel a professional duty to history to never let the “Hand of God” be forgotten? Victor Segovia
My feelings haven’t changed and they won’t. But I’ve learned to live with it better, I’ve learned to get through it and I’m not so annoyed by the memory. You’re just disappointed it happened. It had an influence on the game because we went one down and I think a lot of the players were shocked by what happened. Half the team saw it, half didn’t. I was one of the ones who didn’t. It had a big part to play in the fact we didn’t get switched on again and conceded the second goal. I’m more disappointed because he beat me twice. You’ve got to respect the man and respect what he did for the second goal, and what he did in that game. He was the best player I’ve played against and one that I never really got near.
Maradona’s “wondergoal” – it was really an own goal by you as you did a desperate sliding tackle, wasn’t it? David
If I’d got a touch I’d have raised my hand straight away and admitted it was the best own goal I’d ever scored. He went past Peter Shilton and I managed to get back, but I couldn’t see the ball so I was kind of feeling around him with my left foot. I couldn’t get my right foot across, but I thought I could block it. I was so surprised when he made good contact and put it in the net because I thought: “I’ve got this.” You can see me afterwards on the TV, I’m banging my shinpads, I was so angry. I was more angry about that goal than I was the “Hand of God” goal. So I’d have loved to claim that one. I know it sounds bizarre but it would have been one of my greatest achievements. Would it still have been the greatest goal scored at a World Cup?
In the early 80s you had a brilliant side at Portman Road so I wondered if you have: “If only …” or “What if …” moments about that time. It has always felt to me that Ipswich left another big trophy or two out there. Stooze
We did. The 1980-81 season was arguably the best in our history. We lost the FA Cup semi-final, lost the league title on the last day of the season and then had to play the Uefa Cup final, which thankfully we won. It’s always at the back of your mind that you missed out on what you should have got, which was the treble. We should have done it. But I think the 66-game season was just too much for us, we didn’t have a big squad and struggled with injuries towards the end. But we came really close. Look at the teams Sir Bobby built, we were in Europe for nine seasons out of 10. There’s no particular moment I sit down and dwell on, but you know it’s there, so close but so far.
What was the one quality Bobby Robson had above all others and was he the best manager you played under? Carl Parrish
His man-management was top class. He knew how to get the best from his players, knew what buttons to press and got to know them very quickly. He could wield his strength, he was a really tough guy, but when he was friendly it was lovely. His face lit up and he made you feel really good through that man-management. He always used to say to me: “Whenever I pick you, you always do well.” When someone says that you feel really good about yourself. He knew what to say. But had an abundance of things that worked really well for him. His tactical knowledge, selection of players, the network he built up for the younger players to come through, so many things. He was the most complete manager in my eyes and I still think he’s the best. Wherever he went, home or abroad, he proved himself in a way no English manager has done.
What was it like playing alongside Des Walker with England? And how close were England to winning the World Cup in 1990? Ahmed Kheyre
Des was the best centre-half I played alongside for England; he was unbelievable. He prolonged my international career because he was my pace. You never beat Des Walker. He was OK on the ball, it wasn’t his strength, but he used to give it to people that had great ability in that area so he was very astute. He was very young at the time, but dependable, talked well, shouted, pulled you about, was dominant. He was one of the reasons I made it to Italia 90. As for how close we were, I think the semi-final was the best we played all tournament. As I was walking out I felt so serene, comfortable, like I was in a dream state. It was ne…

Clubs with wealthy proprietors can maintain a loss-making operation but things can be more complex when the supporters carry the can
W hen you walk up from Haydons Road train station to Plough Lane there is a blue AFC Wimbledon billboard that reads “Fan owned football”, directly opposite the site of the old Plough Lane stadium where there are now blocks of flats. There is a memorial to the old Wimbledon FC – a reminder that supporters can often have little say in the running of their club – on the same corner, just up the road from the new Cherry Red Records Stadium.
AFC Wimbledon are one of only two majority fan-owned clubs in the EFL – along with Exeter City – but that makes running a loss-making operation, as 94% of teams in England’s top five tiers are doing according to the State of the Game report, even more challenging. “In other clubs, the owner just puts their hand in their pocket, produces cash,” said Hannah Kitcher, who has been a member of the Dons Trust Board (DTB), which runs AFC Wimbledon, for seven years. “It’s harder when the owners are fans – you can only go to them so many times.”
Kitcher was speaking before kick-off in Saturday’s League One game at home to a Blackpool side dealing with a suspected norovirus outbreak in their squad. A superb arrowed strike from Alistair Smith and some vital late saves from Nathan Bishop ended Wimbledon’s winless run of 10 matches in all competitions. The 1-0 victory moved Johnnie Jackson’s side four points clear of the relegation zone and put a positive spin on a week that started with the fallout from the withdrawal of £87m of proposed investment, leaving the club’s finances even tighter.
Wimbledon made a £2.6m loss in the 2024-25 season – a figure expected to increase by £500,000 when they publish their accounts next month – which, as Kitcher pointed out, is not as loss-making as a number of other clubs in League One. Those clubs voted in the summer to reduce spending limits from 60% to 50% of turnover but now many want to go further to curb the spiralling losses at this level. “It’s an ugly way of running a sport,” said Terry Hunt, a supporter who has been attending matches with his son Billy since AFC Wimbledon were founded in 2002 following the move to Milton Keynes.
Wimbledon returned home to Plough Lane in 2020 but had to create a bond to complete the move and the club still owe £7.5m in debts. In November 2025, the DTB warned that competing in the EFL at their new stadium was “not currently sustainable” under their structure at the time.
The makeup of the club has since changed. Last April, supporters voted in favour of reducing their voting rights from 75% to 50.01% – the same 50+1 model that gives fans the final say on decisions at German clubs – and Wimbledon sought a cash injection. An £87m investment proposal from Sloane Street Capital (SSC), a venture including the sole funder, Omar Mir, and the former Chelsea and England defender Ryan Bertrand, was already being voted on by fans when Mir suddenly walked away last Sunday, citing a change in his investment priorities.
Mir passed Wimbledon’s due diligence tests, but the tech businessman was not a unifying figure. A Josimar report has detailed his “various connections to some of the most influential and controversial figures in football, technology and global security”. The 44-year-old did not attend either of the information evenings at Plough Lane after the proposal was first made in October, instead sending a two-minute video message, which meant fans could not directly ask him about his intention to purchase 90% of the economic rights of a fan-owned football club.
“We really wanted to have some kind of knight in shining armour,” said Niall Couper, a former member of the DTB and author of three books on Wimbledon. “In this case, I personally wasn’t sure how shiny that armour was.” Couper, who raised questions about Mir’s background before his withdrawal, chose not attend the Blackpool game owing to anger from some supporters at the deal collapsing.
But the SSC deal is not completely dead. Bertrand and his remaining SSC partners Stuart Fiertz, Oliver Ward and Hugh Rosen – who would have owned 1.25% each of Wimbledon’s economic rights in the original proposal – have renamed themselves Sloane Street Football and are talking to other potential investors.
In the meantime, the board will seek approval from fans about taking out a loan of up to £3m to “manage the club’s cash position”, but they believe they are currently able to manage it through to the end of this season and into the next. Which division Wimbledon end up in next season remains to be seen – Jackson’s side survived relegation by four points last April and the manager will probably have his hands tied in January.
“I think we’ll probably go down, but bouncing between League Two and League One is absolutely fine by me,” said Billy Hunt. “The main goal is security and making sure we have a football club.”
